The sacryfice of God is a troubled spirit a broken and a contrite hert, O God, shalte thou not despyse.
O be fauourable gracyous vnto Syon, that the walles of Ierusalem maye be buylded,
For when shalt thou be pleased wyth the sacrifice of ryghtuousnes, with the burntofferinges and oblations: then shal they laye bullockes vpon thine alter.
52: To the chaunter, an exortacyon of Dauid when Doeg the Edomite came to Saul, and shewed hym, sayinge: Dauid is come to the house of Ahimelech. Why boastest thou thy self, thou Tyrraunt, that thou canste do myschiefe? Wher as the goodnesse of God endureth yet dayly.
Thy tonge ymagyneth wyckednesse, and with lyes it cutteth like a sharpe rasoure.
Thou loueste vngratiousnesse more then good, to talke of lyes more then ryghtuousnesse. Selah.
Thou louest to speake al wordes that may do hurte. O thou false tonge.
Therfore shall God cleane destroye the, smyte the in peces, pluke the out of thy dwellynge, and rote the out of the lande of the lyuynge. Selah.
The rightuous shal se this, and feare, and laugh him to scorne,
Lo, this is the man, that toke not God for his strength but trusted vnto the multitud of his riches, & was myghty in his wickednes.
As for me, I am lyke a grene olyue tree in the house of God: my truste is in the tender mercy of God for euer and euer.
I wyll alwaye geue thankes vnto the, for that thou hast done: & wil hope in thy name, for thy sayntes lyke it wel.
53: To the chaunter vpon Mahalath, an instruccyon of Dauid. The folysh bodyes saye in their hertes: Tush, there is no God. Corrupte are they & become abhomynable in their wyckednesse: there is not one, that doth good.
God loked downe from heauen vpon the chyldren of men, to se if there were any that would vnderstand, or seke after God.
But they are all gone out of the waye they are al become vnprofitable: ther is none that doth good, no not one.
How can they haue vnderstandynge, that are the worckers of wyckednes, eatynge vp my people as it were breade, and call not vpon God?
They are afrayed, where no feare is: for God breaketh the bones of them that beseige the: thou puttest them to confusion, for God despiseth them.
Oh that the sauynge healthe were geuen vnto Israel out of Sion: Oh that the Lorde woulde delyuer his people out of captiuity. Then shoulde Iacob reioyse, and Israell should be ryght glad.
54: To the chaunter in Neginoth, an instruccyon of Dauyd, when the Zephytes came and sayed vnto Saul: Dauid is hydde amongest vs. Helpe me (O God) for thy names sake, and deliuer me in thy strength.
Heare my prayer (O God) considre the wordes of my mouth.
For straungers are rysen vp agaynst me, and the mighty (which haue not God before their eyes) seke after my soule. Selah.
But lo, God is my helper: it is he that vpholdeth my soule.
He shall reward euel vnto myne enemies and in thy trueth shalt thou destroy them.
A fre will offerynge will I geue the, and prayse thy name O Lorde, because it is so comfortable.
For thou hast deliuered me out of all my trouble, so that myne eye seith his desire vpon myne enemyes.
55: To the chaunter in Neginoth, an instruccion of Dauid. Heare my prayer, O God, and hyde not thy self fro my petycion.
Take hede vnto me & heare me, how piteously I mourne and complayne.
The enemye cryeth so, and the vngodly commeth on so fast: for they are mynded too do me some mischief, so maliciously are they set agaynst me.
My hert is heuy within me, and the feare of death is fallen vpon me.
Fearfulnesse and tremblynge are come vpon me, and an horrible drede hathe ouerwhelmed me.
And I sayde: O that I had wynges lyke a doue, that I might fle somwhere, and be at rest.
Lo, then wolde I get me awaye farre of, and remayne in the wildernesse. Selah.
I wolde make haste to escape, from the stormy wynde and tempest.
Destroye their tonges (O Lorde) and deuyde them, for I se vnrighteousnes & stryfe in the cytye.
Thys goeth daye and nyght aboute the walles, mischief and vyce are in the middest of it.
Wickednesse is therin, disceate and gyle go not out of her stretes.
If it were myne enemye that reuyled me, I could beare it: or if one that ought me euel wyll dyd threaten me, I wolde hyde my self from hym.
But it is thou my companyon, my gyde & myne owne familier frende.
We had swete and secrete communicacion together in the house of God.
Let death come hastely vppon them, and let them goo doune quyck into hell, for wickednes is amonge theym in their dwellynges.
As for me, I will call vnto God, and the Lord shall helpe me.
In the euenynge, mornyng and at noone daye will I mourne and complayne: and he shall heare my voyce.
It is he that deliuereth my soule in peace, from them that laye wayte for me: for they are many agaynst me.
Yea, euen God that endureth for euer, shall heare me, and bring them doune. Selah. For they will not turne: and why? they feare not God.
Yea, they laye handes vpon such as be at peace with hym, & so they breake hys couenaunt.
Their mouthes are softer then butter, & yet haue they battayll in theyr mynde: theyr wordes are smoother then oyle, and yet be they very swerdes.
O cast thy burthen, or care, vpon the Lord he shall norysh the, and not leaue the ryghteous in vnquyetnesse.
But as for them, thou (O God) shalt cast doune into the pytte of destruccion. The bloudthrustye & disceatfull shall not lyue out half their dayes. Neuerthelesse my trust is in the.
56: To the chaunter, vpon the domme stock doue: whiche flyeth ferre of, Michtam of Dauid, when the Phylystynes toke hym in Geth. Be mercifull vnto me (O God) for men will treade me doune: they are dayly fightynge and troublynge me.
Myne enemyes treade me dayly vnder their fete, for they be many that proudly fighte agaynste me.
Neuerthelesse, when I am afrayed, I put my trust in the.
I will comforte my selfe in Gods worde, yea, I will hope in God, & not feare: What can flesh then do vnto me?
They vexe my dayly in my wordes: all that they ymagyne, is to do me euell.
They holde alltogether, & kepe them selues close they marcke my steppes, how they may catch my soule.
But in vayne, for it shall escape them: and why? thou (O God) in thy dyspleasure shalt cast doune suche people.
Thou tellest my flytynges, thou puttest my teares in thy bottel, and numbrest them.
When soeuer I call vpon the, myne enemyes are put to flight: whereby I knowe that thou art my God.
In Goddes worde wyll I reioyse, in the Lordes worde wyll I comforte me.
Yea, in God do I trust, and am not afraied what can man than do vnto me?
Vnto the (O god) wil I paye my vowes, vnto the wyll I geue thankes and prayse.
For thou haste delyuered my soule from death, and my fete frome fallynge, that I may walke before God in the lyght of the lyuyng.
57: To the Chaunter destroy not Michtam of Dauid, when he fledde from Saull into the caue. Be mercyfull vnto me, O God, be mercyfull vnto me, for my soule trusteth in the: and vnder the shadow of thy winges shal be my refuge, vntyll wyckednes be ouer past.
I call vnto God the moste hyest, euen the God that shal helpe me vp agayne.
He shal send from heauen, and saue me from the reproue of him that would swalowe my vp. Selah. This shall God sende, for his mercye and faythfulnes sake.
I lye wyth my soule among the cruel lions euen among the chyldren of men, whose teeth are speares and arrowes, and their tonge a sherpe sweard.
Set vp thy selfe, O God, aboue the heauens, and thy glory aboue al the earthe.
They haue layed a net for my fete, and pressed doune my soule: they haue dygged a pytte before me, and are fallen into it them selues. Selah.
My hert is redy, O God, my herte is ready to synge and geue prayse.
Awake, O my glorye, awake lute and harpe, I my selfe wil awake ryght early.
I wil geue thanckes vnto the, O Lorde, amonge the people, I wyll synge prayses vnto the among the Heithen.
For the greatnes of thy mercye reacheth vnto the heauens, and thy faythfulnes vnto the cloudes.
Set vp thy selfe, O God, aboue the heauens, and thi glory aboue al the earth.
58: To the chaunter Destroye not Michtam of Dauid. If youre myndes be vpon righteousnes in deede, then iudge the thyng that is ryght, O ye sonnes of men,
But ye ymagyn mischefe in youre hertes and youre handes deale with wickednes.
The vngodly are froward, euen from their mothers wombe: as soone as they be borne, they go a stray and speake lyes.
They are as furyous as the serpent, euen lyke the deaf Ader that stoppeth her eares.
That she shoulde not heare the voyce of the charmer, charme he neuer so wisely.
Breake their teeth (O god) in their mouthes, smite the chaft bones of the lions whelpes in sonder, O Lord.
That they maye fall awaye, lyke water that runneth a pace: and that when they shote their arrowes, they maye be broken.
Let them consume away lyke a snaile, and lyke the vntymely frute of a woman, and let them not se the sunne.
Or euer your thorns be sharpe, the wrath shall take them awaye quicke, like a stormy wynde.
The ryghteous shal reioyse when he seith the vengeaunce, and shall washe hys fete in the bloud of the vngodly.
So that men shall saye, verelye there is a rewarde for the righteous: doutles, there is a God that iudgeth the earth.
59: To the chaunter destroye not Michtam of Dauid, when Saull sende to watche the house, to thintent to kyll hym. Delyuer me fro myne enemyes (O my God) and defende me from them that rise vp against me.
O delyuer me from the wycked doers, and saue me from the bloudthursty men.
For lo, they lye wayting for my soule: the mighty men are gathered together agaynste me, withoute any offence or faulte of me, O Lorde.
They runne, & prepare them selfes, without my faute: Arise, come thou helpe me, and beholde.
Stande vp O Lord God of hostes, thou God of Israel to viset all Heythen: be not mercifull vnto theym that offende of malicious wyckednesse. Selah.
Let them go to and fro, and runne aboute the cytye, houlynge lyke dogges.
Beholde, they speake (agaynste me) wyth their mouth, swerdes are vnder their lippes for who reproueth them?
But thou (O Lorde) shalte haue theim in derision, thou shalte laugh all Heythen too scorne.
My strength do I ascrybe vnto the, for thou (O God) art my defender.
God sheweth me his goodnes plenteously, God letteth me se my desyre vppon myne enemyes.
Slaye them not, leste my people forget it: but scatre them abroade with thy power, & put them doune, O Lord my defence.
For the synne of their mouth, for the wordes of their lyppes, & because of their pryde, let them be taken: and why? their preachyng is of cursing and lyes.
Consume them in thy wrath, consume them that they maye perishe, and knowe that it is God, whyche ruleth in Iacob and in all the worlde. Selah.
Set them go to and fro, and runne aboute the cytye, houlyng lyke dogges.
Let them runne here and there for meate, and grudge when they haue not ynough.
As for me, I will synge of thy power, and prayse thy mercy by tymes in the mornyng: for thou art my defence & refuge in the tyme of my trouble.
Vnto the (O my strengthe) wyll I singe, for thou (O God) art my defence, & my mercifull God.
60: To the chaunter, vpon the rose of wytnesse Michtam of Dauid, for too teache when he fought agaynst Syria of Mesopotania, & Syria of Zoba: and when Ioab turned backe, and slue .xij. thousand Edomytes. in the valley of Salt. O God, thou that hast cast vs out and scatered vs abroade, thou that hast bene so sore displeased at vs, comforte vs agayne.
Thou that hast remoued the lande & deuided it, heale the sores therof, for it shaketh.
Thou hast shewed thy people heuy thinges, thou hast geuen vs a drynke of wyne, that we slombre with all.
Yet hast thou geuen a token for suche as feare the, that they maye caste it vp in the trueth. Selah.
That thy beloued myghte be delyuered, healpe them wyt thy ryghthande, and heare me.
God hath spoken in his Sanctuary (which thing reioyseth me) I wyll deuyde Sichem, and meate aut the valley of Suchoth.
Galaad is myne, Manasses is myne, Ephraim is the strength of myne head, Iuda is my Captayne.
Moab is my washpotte, ouer Edom will I stretche oute my shoue, Phylystea shalbe glad of me.
Who will leade me into the strong cytie? Who will bryng me into Edom?
Shalt not thou do it O God, thou that hast cast out: thou God, that wenteste not out with our hostes?
O be thou our helpe in trouble, for vayne is the helpe of man.
Thorow God we shal do great actes, for it is he that shall treade downe oure enemies
61: To the chaunter vpon Neginoth, of Dauid Heare my crying (O god) geue hede vnto my prayer.
From the endes of the earth will I call vnto the, when my herte is in trouble:
Oh sette me vp vpon an hye rocke. For thou art my hope, a strong tower for me agaynst the enemye.
I wyll dwell in thy tabernacle for euer, that I maye be safe vnder the couerynge of thy wynges. Selah.
For thou, O Lord, hast harde my desyres, thou hast geuen an heretage vnto those that feare thy name.
Thou shalte graunte the Kynge a longe lyfe, that his yeares may endure thorow out all generacyons.
That he maye dwel before God for euer: Oh let thy louynge mercy and faythfulnes preserue hym.
So wyl I al away syng prayses vnto thy name, that I may dayly perfourme my vowes.
62: To the chaunter, for by Iduthun a Psalme of Dauyd. My soule wayteth onely vpon God, for of hym commeth my helpe.
He only is my strength, my saluation, my defence, so that I shal not greatly fall.
How longe wyll ye ymagyn myschiefe agaynste euerye man? ye shalbe slayne all the sorte of you: yea as a tottrynge wall shall ye be, and lyke a broken hedge.
Their deuyce is only how to put hym out, their delite is in lyes: they geue good wordes wyth their mouth, but curse wyth the herte. Selah.
Neuerthelesse, my soule abideth only vpon God, for he is my God.
He only is my strength my saluacion, and my defence: so that I shall not fal.
In God is my helth, my glory, my might, and in God is my trust.
O put your trust in him alway (ye people) poure oute youre hertes before hym, for God is our hope. Selah.
As for men, they are but vayne, men are dysceatfull: vpon the weyghtes they are all together lyghter than vanitye it selfe.
O trust not in wronge and robbery, geue not youre selues vnto vanitye: if ryches encrease, set not your herte vpon them.
God spake once a worde, twyse haue I hearde the same: that power belongeth vnto God
That thou Lorde arte mercyfull, and that thou rewardeste euerye man accordynge to his worckes.
63: A Psalme of Dauid, when he was in the wildernes of Iuda. O God, thou art my God: earlye wyll I seke the. My soule thrusteth for the, my flesh longeth after the in a baren and drye lande wher no water is.
Thus do I loke for the in thy Sanctuary, that I myght beholde thy power and glorye,
For thy louynge kyndnesse is bettrr then lyfe, my lyppes shall prayse the.
As longe as I lyue wyll I magnyfye the and lyft vp my handes in thy name.
My soule is satisfied euen as it were with mary and fatnesse, when my mouth prayseth the with ioyful lyps.
In my bedde wyll I remember the, and when I wake my talkynge shalbe of the.
For thou hast bene my helper, and vnder the shadow of thy wynges wyl I reioyse.
My soule hangeth vpon the, thy ryghte hande vpholdeth me.
They seke after my soule, but in vayne, for they shall go vnder the earth.
They shall fall into the swerd, and be a porcyon for foxes.
But the Kynge shall reioyse in God: all they that sweare by him, shalbe commended for the mouth of lyers shalbe stopped.
64: To the chaunter a Psalme of Dauid. Heare my voice, O God, in my complaynte, preserue my lyfe from feare of the enemye.
Hide me from the gathering together of the frowarde, from the heape of wycked doers.
Which whet their tonges lyke a sweard, and shote wyth their veneymous words like as with arowes.
That they maye preuely hurt the innocent sodenly to hyt him wythout any feare.
They haue deuysed myschefe, and communed amonge them selues, how they may laye snares: tush (saye they) who shall se them?
They ymagyn wyckednes, and kepe it secrete amonge them selues, euerye man in the depe of his herte.
But God shal sodenly shote wyth an arow that they shalbe wounded.
Yea their owne tonges shall make them fall, in somuch that who so seyth them, shall laugh them to scorne.
And all men that se it shal saye: thys hath God done, for they shall perceyue that it is hys worcke.
The righteous shal reioyse in the Lorde, and put his trust in him: and all they that are true of hert, shalbe glad therof.
65: To the chaunter, a Psalme and song of Dauid. Thou, O God art, praised in Syon, and vnto the is the vow perfourmed.
Thou hearest the praier, therfore commeth all fleshe vnto the.
Oure misededes preuaile agayust vs, Oh be thou mercyfull vnto our synnes.
Blessed is the man whom thou chosest and receauest vnto the, that he may dwell in thy courtes: he shalbe satisfied wyth the pleasures of thy house, euen of thy holy temple.
Heare vs, according vnto thy wonderfull rightuousnesse, O God oure saluation: thou that art the hope of all the endes of the earth, and of the broade sea.
Which in his strength setteth fast the mountaynes, and is gyrded aboute wyth power.
Which stilleth the ragynge of the sea, the roarynge of his waues, and the woodnes of the people.
They that dwell in the vttermoste partes are afrayed at thy tokens, thou makest both the mornyng and euenyng starres to prayse the.
Thou visitest the earth, thou waterest it. and makest it very plenteous. The riuer of god is ful of waters, thou preparest man hys corne, and thus thou prouydeste for the earth.
Thou waters, her forowes, thou breakest the harde clottes thereof, thou makest it softe with the droppes of rayne, and blessest the increase of it.
Thou crownest the yeare wyth thy good and thy fotsteppes droppe fatnesse.
The dwellinges of the wildernes are fat also, that they droppe wyth all: and the lytle hylles are pleasaunt on euerye syde.
The foldes are full of shepe, the valleyes stande so thicke with corne that they laughe and synge.
66: To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauyd. O be ioyfull in God, all ye landes,
synge prayses vnto the honoure of his name, make hys prayse to be gloryous.
Saye vnto God: O howe wonderful are thy worckes? thorowe the greatenesse of thy power shall thine enemyes be confounded.
O that all the worlde woulde worshippe the, synge of the, and prayse thy name. Selah
O come hyther and beholde the worckes of God, which is so wonderful in his doinges amonge the chyldren of men.
He turned the sea into drye lande, so that they wente thorow the water on fote: therefore wyll we reioyse in him.
He ruleth wyth hys power for euer, hys eyes beholde the people: the rennagates shall not be able to exalte them selues. Selah.
O magnyfye oure God, ye people, make the voyce of his prayse to be hearde.
Whych holdeth oure soule in life, and suffreth not our fete to slyppe.
For thou, O God, hast proued vs, thou hast tryed vs lyke as syluer is tryed.
Thou hast broughht vs into captyuyty, & layed trouble vpon oure loynes.
Thou haste suffred men to ryde ouer oure heades, we went thorow fyre and water, but thou hast broughte vs out, and refreshed vs.
Therfore wyll I go into thy house wyth brentoffrynges, to paye the my vowes,
which I promysed with my lippes, and spake wyth my mouth, when I was in trouble.
I wyll offer vnto the fat brentsacrifyces wyth the smoke of rammes, I wyl offer bullockes and goates. Selah.
O come hither, and herken, all ye that feare God, I wyll tell you, what he hath done for my soule.
I called vnto hym wyth my mouthe, and gaue hym prayses wyth my toung.
If I enclyne vnto wyckednesse wyth my herte, the Lorde wyll not heare me.
Therfore God hath herde me, and consydred the voyce of my prayer.
Praysed be God, which hath not cast out my prayer, ner turned his mercy fro me.
67: To the chaunter, in Neginoth, a Psalm and songe. God be mercyfull vnto vs, blesse vs, and shewe the lyght of hys countenaunce vpon vs. Selah
That we maye knowe thy waye vpon earth, thy sauynge helth among al Heathen.
Let the people prayse the, O God, yea let all people prayse the.
O let the people reioyse and be glad, that thou iudgest the folke ryghtuouslye, and gouernest the nacions vpon earth.
Let the people prayse the, O God, let al people prayse the.
God, euen oure owne God, geue vs hys blessynge, that the earth maye brynge forth her encrease.
God blesse vs, and let all the endes of the world feare hym.
68: To the chaunter, a Psalm and song. of Dauid. Let God aryse, so shall hys enemyes be scattered, and they that hate hym, shall flee before hym.
Lyke as the smoke vanysheth, so shalt thou dryue them away: and lyke as waxe melteth at the fyre so shal the vngodly perysh at the presence of God.
But the ryghtuous shalbe glad and reioyce before God, they shalbe mery and ioyfull.
Oh synge vnto God, synge prayses vnto his name: magnify hym that rydeth aboute the heauens (whose name is the Lord) & reioyce before hym.
He is a father of the fatherlesse, he is a defender of widdowes: euen God in his holy habytacyon.
He is the God that maketh men to be of one mynde in a house, and bryngeth the presoners out of captyuity in due season, but let the rennagates contynue in scarcenesse.
O God, when thou wenteste forth before the people, when thou wentest thorowe the wyldernesse. Selah.
The earth shoke, and the heauens dropped at the presence of God in Sinai, at the presence of God, whyche is the God of Israell.
Thou O God sendest a gracyous raine vpon thyne enherytaunce, and refreshest it when it is dry.
That thy beastes may dwel therin, which thou of thy goodnesse haste prepared for the poore.
The Lorde shall geue the worde, wyth great hostes of Euangelystes.
Kynges wyth their armyes shall fle, and they of the housholde shall deuyde the spoile
If so be that ye lye amonge the pales, the doues fethers shalbe couered with syluer, & her wynges of the colour of golde.
When the Almyghty setteth Kynges vpon the earth, it shalbe cleare euen in the darkne
The hyll of Basan is Gods hyl, the hil of Basan is a plenteous hyl.
Why hoppe ye so, ye greate hylles? It pleaseth God to dwell vpon thys hyll yea the Lorde wyll abide in it for euer.
The charettes of God are many .M. tymes thousande, the Lorde is among them in the holy Sinai.
Thou art gone vp an hye, thou hast ledde captiuitie captiue, and receyued gyftes for men: Yea, euen for thyne enemyes, that they might dwell with the Lord God.
Praysed be the Lord dayly, euen the God whiche helpeth vs, & poureth hys benefites vpon vs. Selah.
The God that is our sauiour, euen God the Lord by whome we escape death.
The God that smyteth the enemies vpon the heades and vpon the heary scalpes: such as go on styll in their wickednes.
The Lorde hath sayde: some wil I bryng agayne from Basan, some wyll I brynge agayne from the depe of the sea.
That thy fote may be dipped in the bloud of thyne enemyes, and that thy dogges may licke it vp.
It is well sene, O God, how thou goest, howe thou my God and kynge goest in the Sanctuary.
The singers go before, and then the mynstrels amonge the maydens with the tymbrels.
O geue thankes vnto God the Lorde in the congregacion, for the welles of Israel.
There lytle Beniamin, the princes of Iuda, the princes of Zabulon, & the princes of Nephthaly beare rule amonge them.
Thy God hath commytted strength vnto the, stablyshe the thynge, O God, that thou hast wrought in vs.
For thy temples sake at Hierusalem shall kynges brynge presentes vnto the.
Reproue the beastes amonge the reedes, the heape of bulles with the calues: those that dryue for money. Oh scatre the people that delite in battaile.
The princes shall come out of Egipt, the Morians land shall stretch out her handes vnto God.
Synge vnto God, O ye kyngedomes of the earth: O syng prayses vnto the Lorde. Selah.
Which sitteth in the heauens ouer all from the beginnynge: Lo, he shall sende oute hys voyce, yea, and that a mighty voyce.
Ascrybe ye the power vnto God, his glory is in Israel, and his might in the cloudes.
God is wonderfull in his Sanctuary, he is the God of Israel, he will geue strength and power vnto hys people. Blessed be God.
69: To the chaunter vpon Sosanim of Dauid. Helpe me, O god, for the waters are come in, euen vnto my soule.
I stycke fast in the depe myre where no ground is: I am come into depe waters, and the floudes wyll drowne me.
I am weery of crying, my throte is drye, my sight fayleth me, for waytinge so longe, vpon my God.
They that hate me without a cause, are mo then the heeres of my head: they that are myne enemyes & wolde destroye me giltlesse are mighty: I am fayne to paye the thinges that I neuer toke.
God thou knowest my simplenesse, and my faultes are not hyd from the.
Let not them that trust in the, O Lord God of hoostes, be ashamed for my cause: let not those that seke the, be confounded thorowe me, O God of Israel.
And why? for thy sake do I suffre reprofe, shame couereth my face.
I am become a straunger vnto my brethren, and an aleaunt vnto my mothers chyldren.
For the zele of thyne house hath euen eaten me, and the rebukes of them that rebuked the, is fallen vpon me.
I wepte and chastened my selfe with fastyng, and that was turned to my reprofe.
I put on a sacke cloth, and therefore they iested vpon me.
They that sate in the gate, spake agaynste me, & the dronkardes made songes vpon me.
But Lorde I made my prayer vnto the in an acceptable tyme. Heare me, O God, with thy great mercy and sure helpe.
Take me out of the myre, that I sinke not Oh let me be deliuered from them that hate me, and out of the depe waters.
Lest the water floud drowne me, that the depe swalowe me not vp, and that the pytte shut not her mouth vpon me.
Heare me, O Lord, for thy louyng kyndnesse is comfortable: turne the vnto me according vnto thy great mercy.
Hyde not thy face from thy seruaunt, for I am in trouble: O haste the to helpe me.
Drawe nye vnto my soule, & saue it: Oh deliuer me because of myne enemyes.
Thou knowest my reprofe, my shame & my dishonoure: myne aduersaries are all in thy sight.
The rebuke breaketh my herte, and maketh me heuy: I loke for some to haue pytye vpon me, but ther is no man: and for some to comforte me, but I fynde none.
They gaue me gall to eate, & when I was thurstye, they gaue me vinegar to dryncke.
Let their table be made a snare to take them selues with all, an occasyon to fall and a reward vnto them.
Let their eyes be blinded, that they se not: and euer bow downe their backes.
Power out thyne indignacyon vpon them, and let thy wrathfull dyspleasure take holde of them.
Let theyr habytacyon be voyd, and no man to dwel in ther tentes.
For they persecute hym whom thou hast smytten, and besyde thy woundes they haue geuen him mo.
Let them fall from one wyckednesse to another, and not come into thy ryghtuousnesse.
Let them be wyped out of the boke of the lyuynge, and not be wrytten amonge the ryghtuous.
As for me, I am poore and in heuines, let thy helpe defend me O God.
That I may praise the name of God, with a songe and magnyfye it wyth thanckesgeuynge.
Thys shall please the Lord better then a bullocke, that hath hornes and hoofes.
O consyder this and be glad (ye that be in aduersytye) seke after God, and youre soule shall lyue.
For the Lorde heareth the poore, and despyseth not hys priesoners.
Let heauen and earth praise him, the sea & all that moueth ther in.
For God wyll saue Syon, and buyld the cityes of Iuda, that men may dwel ther, and haue them in possession.
The sede of his seruauntes shall inherette it, and they that loue hys name shall dwell therein.
70: The chaunter, of Dauid to bryng to remembraunce. Hast the, O God, to deliuer me, and to helpe me, O Lord.
Let them be shamed and confounded that seke after my soule let them be turned backward and put to confusyon, that wysh my euyl.
Let them sone be broughte to shame, that crye ouer me, there there.
But let all those that seke the, be ioyfull & gladde in the: and let al suche as delyte in thy sauynge health, saye alwaye: the Lorde be praysed.
As for me, I am poore and in misery, hast the God for to helpe me. Thou art my helpe, my redemer and my God: Oh make no long tarying.
71: In the, O Lord, is my trust, let me neuer be put to confusyon,
but rydde me, and delyuer me thorow thy ryghtuousnesse: enclyne thyne eare vnto me, and helpe me.
Be thou my strong hold (wher vnto I may all waye fle) thou that hast promised to helpe me: for thou art my house of defence and my castell.
Deliuer me, O my God, out of the hand of the vngodly, oute of the hande of the vnryghtuous and cruell man.
For thou, O Lord God, art the thing that I long for, thou art my hope euen fro my youth.
I haue leaned vpon the euer sence I was borne, thou art he that toke me out of my mothers wombe therfore is my prayse all waye of the.
I am become a wonder vnto the multytude, but my sure trust is in the.
Oh let my mouth be filled with thy praise and honour all the day long.
Cast me not away in myne old age forsake me not when my strength fayleth me.
For myne enemyes speake agaynst me & they that laye wayte for my soule, take their councell together,
sayinge: God hath forsaken hym, persecute hym, take hym, for there is none to helpe hym.
Go not farre fro me, O God: my God, haste the to helpe me.
Let them be confounded and perysh, that are agaynste my soule: let theym be couered with shame and dishonoure, that seke too do me euell.
As for me, I wil paciently abyde alwaye, and will euer encrease thy prayse.
My mouth shall speake of thy righteousnesse and sauyng health all the day longe, for I knowe no ende therof.
Let me go in (O Lorde God) and I wyll make mencion of thy power and righteousnesse onely.
Thou, O God, haste learned me fro my youth vp vntyll now, therfore wyll I tell of thy wonderous workes.
Forsake me not, O GOD, in myne olde age, when I am gray headed: vntyll I haue shewed thyne arme vnto chylders chyldren, and thy power to all them that are yet for to come.
Thy righteousnes, O God, is very hye, thou that doest great thinges: O God, who is lyke vnto the?
O what great troubles and aduersityes hast thou shewed me? and yet dyddest thou turne and refreshe me: yea, & broughtest me from the depe of the earth agayn.
Thou hast brought me to great honoure, and comforted me on euery syde.
Therfore wil I prayse the and thy faythfulnesse, O God, playing vpon the lute, vnto the will I singe vpon the harpe, O thou holy one of Israell.
My lippes wolde fayne singe prayses vnto the: and so wolde my soule, whom thou hast deliuered.
My tongue talketh of thy righteousnesse all the daye longe, for they are confounded and brought vnto shame, that soughte to do me euell.
72: Of Salomon. Geue the king thy iudgement, O God, and thy righteousnesse vnto the kynges sonne.
That he maye gouerne thy people accordynge vnto ryght and defende thy poore.
That the mountaynes maye brynge peace, and the litle hylles righteousnesse vnto the people.
He shall kepe the symple folke by theyr ryght, defende the chyldren of the poore, and punish the wronge doer.
Thou shalt be feared as longe as the sunne and moone endureth, from one generacyon to another.
He shall come doune lyke the rayne into a fleise of wolle, & like the droppes that water the earth.
In hys tyme shall righteousnesse florysh, yea, and aboundaunce of peace, so longe as the moone endureth.
Hys dominion shalbe from the one sea to the other, & from the floud vnto the worldes ende.
They that dwell in the wyldernes shall knele before him, & his enemyes shal licke the dust.
The kynges of the sea & of the Iles shall bringe presentes, the kynges of Araby and Saba shall offre gyftes.
All kynges shall worshyppe hym, and all Heathen shall do hym seruyce.
For he shall delyuer the poore when he cryeth, and the neady that hath no helpe.
He shalbe fauorable to the simple & poore, he shall preserue the soules of suche as be in aduersitie.
He shall delyuer their soules from extorcyon and wrong, and deere shall their bloud be in hys sight.
He shall lyue, and vnto hym shalbe geuen of the golde of Arabia: Prayer shalbe made euer vnto hym, and daylye shall he be praysed.
There shalbe an heape of corne in the earth hye vpon the hilles, his frute shal shake like Libanus, and shalbe grene in the cytye, lyke grasse vpon the earth.
Hys name shal endure for euer, his name shall remayne vnder the sunne amonge the posterites, which shalbe blessed thorow him and all the Heathen shall prayse hym.
Blessed be the Lorde God, euen the God of Israell, whiche onely doeth wonderous thinges.
And blessed be the name of his maiesty for euer, and al landes be fulfilled with his glory. Amen, Amen.
Here ende the prayers of Dauid the sonne of Iesse.
73: A Psalme of Asaph. O how louyng is God vnto Israel, to suche as are of a cleane hert?
Neuerthelesse my fete were almost gone, my treadynges had well nye slypte.
And why? I was greued at the wicked, to se the vngodly in suche prosperitie.
For they are in no parell of deathe, but stande fast lyke a palace.
They come in no misfortune lyke other folke, neither are they plaged like other men.
And this is the cause that they be so puft vp in pryde, and ouerwhelmed with crueltie & vnrighteousnesse.
Their eyes swell for fatnesse, they do euen what they lyst.
Corrupte are they, and speake blasphemyes maliciouslye, proude and presumpteous are their wordes.
They stretche forth their mouthe vnto the heauen, and their tongue goeth thorow the worlde.
Therfore fall the people vnto them, and thereout sucke they no small auauntage.
Tush (saye they) howe shoulde God perceiue it? is there knowlege in the most hyest?
Lo, these are the vngodly, these prospere in the worlde, these haue ryches in possession.
Shoulde I then clense my herte in vayne (thougt I) and washe my handes in innocency?
Wherefore shoulde I be then punyshed dayly, & be chastened euery mornynge?
Yea, I had almoost also sayd euen as they: but lo, then shoulde I haue condemned the generacion of thy chyldren.
Then thought I, to vnderstande this, but it was to harde for me.
Vntyll I wente into the Sanctuary of God, and considred the ende of these men.
Namely, how thou hast set them in a slippery place, that thou mayst cast them doune headlinges and destroye them.
O how sodenly do they consume, perysh, and come to a fearful ende?
Yea, euen like as a dreame when one awaketh, so makest thou their ymage too vanysh out of the cytye.
Thus my hert was greued, and it wente euen thorow my reynes.
So folysh was I and ignoraunte, and as it were a beast before the.
Neuerthelesse I am al waye by the, thou holdest me by my right hande.
Thou leadest me with thy counsayll, and afterwarde receyuest me vnto glory.
O what is there prepared for me in heauen? there is nothinge vpon earthe, that I desyre in comparyson of the.
My fleash & my hert fayleth, but God is the strength of my herte, and my porcion for euer.
For lo, they that forsake the shall perysh: thou destroyest all them that committe fornicacion agaynst the.
But it is good for me, to holde me fast by God, to put my trust in the Lorde God, and to speake of all thy workes.
74: An instruccion of Asaph. O God, wherfore doest thou cast vs so cleane away? why is thy wrath so hoote agaynste the shepe of thy pasture?
O thynke vpon thy congregacion, whome thou hast purchased from the beginnyng: the stafe of thyne enheritaunce, whome thou hast redemed, euen this hyll of Sion wherein thou dwellest.
Treade vpon them with thy fete, and cast them doune to the grounde, for the enemye hath destroyed altogether in the Sanctuary.
Thyne aduersaries roare in thy houses, & set vp their banners for tokens.
Men may se the axes glyster aboue, lyke as those that hewe in the wood.
They cut doune all the syelyng worke of the Sanctuary with bylles and axes.
They haue set fyre vpon the Sanctuary, they haue defyled the dwellyng place of thy name, euen vnto the grounde.
Yea, they say in their hertes: let vs spoyle them altogether, thus haue they brent vp all the houses of God in the lande.
We se oure tokens no more, there is not one Prophet more, no not one that vnderstandeth any more.
O God, how long shall the aduersary do this dishonoure? how longe shall the enemy blaspheme thy name? for euer?
Why withdrawest thou thine hand? why pluckest thou not thy right hande out of thy bosome, to consume thyne enemyes?
But God is my Kynge of olde, the helpe that is done vpon earth, he doth it hym selfe.
Thou deuidest the sea thorow thy power thou breakest the heades of the dragons in the waters.
Thou smitest the heades of Leuiathan in peces, and geuest him to be meate for people in the wyldernes.
Thou diggest vp welles and brokes, thou dryest vp myghty waters.
The daye is thyne, and the nyght is thine thou hast prepared the lightes and the sunne.
Thou hast set all the borders of the earth, thou hast made both sommer and winter.
Remember this, O Lord, how the enemy rebuketh, and howe the folyshe people blaspheme thy name.
O delyuer not the soule of thy turtle doue vnto the beastes, and forget not the congregacyon of the poore for euer.
Loke vpon the couenaunte, for the darcke houses of the earth are full of wyckednesse.
O let not the symple go awaye ashamed: for the poore and nedy geue prayses vnto thy name.
Aryse, O God, and mayntaine thine own cause, remembre howe the folyshe man blasphemeth the daylye.
Forget not the voyce of thyne enemyes, for the presumptyon of them that hate the, increaseth euer more and more
75: To the chaunter destroye not, a Psalme and song of Asaph. Vnto the, O God, wil we geue thankes, yea vnto the wyll we geue thanckes, and seynge thy name is so ny, we wil tel of thy wonderous worckes.
When I maye get a conuenyent tyme, I shall iudge accordyng vnto ryght.
The earh is weake and al that is therein, but I beare vp her pyllers.
I sayde vnto the madde people, deale not so madly, and to the vngodly set not vp your hornes.
Set not vp your hornes on hie, and speake not wyth a styfe necke.
For promocyon commeth neyther from the East ner from the weste, ner yet from the wyldernesse
And why? God is the Iudge: he putteth downe one, and setteth vp another.
For in the hand of the Lord ther is a cup full of strong wyne, and he poureth oute of the same: As for the dregges therof, al the vngodly of the earth shall dryncke them, and sucke them oute.
But I wyll talke of the God of Iacob, & prayse him for euer.
Al the hornes of the vngodly wil I breake and the hornes of the ryghtuous shall be exalted.
76: To the chaunter, in Neginoth, a Psalm and songe of Asaph. In Iuda is God knowne, hys name is great in Israel.
At Salem is hys tabernacle, and his dwellinge in Sion.
Ther breaketh he the arowes of the bow, the shylde, the swearde, and the whole battaylle, Selah.
Thou art of more honour and might then the hylles of robbers.
The proude shalbe robbed and slepe their slepe, and the myghtye shalbe able to do nothyng with their handes.
When thou rebukest them, O God of Iacob, both the charrettes and horsemen shall fal on slepe.
Thou art fearful, for who maye abyde in thi sight, when thou art angry?
When thou lettest thy iudgment be heard from heauen, the earth trembleth and is stil.
Yea when God aryseth to geue iudgment and to helpe all them that be in aduersyty vpon earth. Selah.
When thou punyshest one man, he muste knowledge that thou arte readye to punyshe other mo.
Loke what ye promise vnto the Lord your God, se that, ye kepe it, all ye that be rounde about him: brynge presentes vnto hym that ought to be feared.
Which taketh awaye the breth of Prynces, and is wonderfull amonge the Kynges of the earth.
77: To the chaunter, for Iduthun. a Psalme of Asaph. I cryed vnto God wyth my voyce, yea vnto God cryed I wyth my voyce, and he hearde me.
In the tyme of my trouble I soughte the Lorde, I helde vp myne handes vnto him in the night season, for my soule refused all other comforte.
When I was in heuinesse, I thought vpon God: when my hert was vexed, then dyd I speake Selah.
Thou heldest myne eyes wakyng, I was so feble, that I coulde not speake.
Then remembred I the tymes of old, and the yeares that were past.
I called to remembraunce my song in the night, I communed wyth myne owne herte, and sought out my spirite.
Wyll the Lorde cast out for euer? Wyl he be no more intreated?
Is hys mercye cleane gone? Is hys promyse come vtterlye to an ende for euermore?
Hath the Lord forgotten to be gracyous? Or, hath he shut vp hys louynge kyndnes in dyspleasure? Selah.
At the last, I came to thys poynte, that I thought: O why art thou so folysh? the right hande of the moost hyest can chaunge all.
Therefore wyll I remembre the worckes of the Lorde, and call to mynde thy wonders of olde tyme.
I wyll speake of all thy worckes, and my talkynge shalbe of thy doynges.
Thy waye, O God, is holye: who is so great and myghty as God?
Thou arte the God that doeth wonders, thou hast declared thy power amonge the people
Thou wyth thyne arme hast delyuered thy people, euen the sonnes of Iacob and Ioseph. Selah.
The waters saw the, O God, the waters sawe the, & were afrayed, the deapthes were moued.
The thicke cloudes poured out water, the cloudes thondered, and thyne arowes went abroade.
The thonder was hearde rounde aboute, the lyghtenynges shone vpon the grounde, the earth was moued and shoke wyth al.
Thy waye was in the sea, and thy pathes in the greate waters, yet coulde noman know thy fotesteppes.
Thou leddeste thy people lyke a flocke of shepe, by the hande of Moyses and Aaron.
78: An instruccyon of Asaph. Heare my lawe, O my people, enclyne your eares vnto the wordes of my mouth.
I wyll open my mouth in parables, and speake of thynges of olde.
Whych we haue herde and knowne, and such as our fathers haue told vs.
That we shoulde not hyde them from the chyldren of the generations to come: but to shewe the honoure of the Lorde, hys myghte and wonderfull worckes that he hath done.
He made a couenaunte wyth Iacob, and gaue Israel a lawe, whiche he commaunded oure forefathers to teache their chyldren.
That their posterytye myghte knowe it, and the chyldren whych were yet vnborne. To thintent that when they came vp they myghte shewe their chyldren the same.
That they also myghte put their truste in God, & not to forget what he had done, but to kepe his commaundementes,
And not to be as their forefathers, a froward and ouerthwarte generatyon, a generation that set not their herte a ryghte, and whose spirite was not true towarde God.
Lyke as the chyldren of Ephraim, which beyng harnessed and carieng bowes, turned them selues backe in tyme of battayl.
They kept not the couenant of god, and wold not walke in his law.
They forgate what he had done, and the wonderfull workes that he had shewed for them.
Maruelous thynges dyd he in the sighte of our fathers in the lande of Egipt, euen in the felde of Zoan.
He deuided the sea & let them go thorowe it, & made the waters to stande like a wall.
In the daye tyme he ledde them with a cloude, and all the night thorow with a light of fyre.
He cloaue the harde rockes in the wildernesse, & gaue them drynke therof, as it hadde bene out of the great deapth.
He brought waters out of the stony rock, so that they gusshed out lyke the ryuers.
Yet for all this they synned agaynste hym, and prouoked the moost hyest in the wyldernes.
They tempted God in their hertes, and requyred meate for their lust.
For they spoke agaynst God, & sayde: yea yea, God shall prepare a table in the wildernesse, shall he?
Lo, he smote the stony rocke, that the watery streames gusshed out, and the streames flowed with all: but how can he geue bread and prouyde flesh for hys people?
When the Lord hearde this, he was wroth so the fyre was kyndled in Iacob, and heauy displeasure agaynst Israel.
Because they beleued not in God, & putte not their trust in hys helpe.
So he commaunded the cloudes aboue, & opened the dores of heauen.
He rayned doune Manna vpon them for to eate, and gaue them bread from heauen.
Then eate they aungels fode, for he sentte them meate ynough.
He caused the East wynd to blowe vnder the heauen, & thorow hys power he brought in the South wynde.
He made flesh to raine vpon them as thicke as dust, and fethered foules like as the sande of the sea.
He let it fall amonge their tentes rounde about theyr habitacions.
So they eate, and were fylled, for he gaue them their owne desyre.
They were not disapoynted of their lust. But whyle the meate was yet in their mouthes:
the heuy wrath of God came vpon them, slewe the welthiest of them, & smote doune the chosen men of Israel.
But for all this they sinned yet more, and beleued not hys wonderous workes.
Therfore their dayes were consumed in vanyte, and sodenly their yeares were gone.
When he slewe them, they sought hym, & turned them early vnto God.
They thoughte then that God was theyr succour, and that the hye God was their redemer.
Neuerthelesse they dyd but flatter him in their mouthes, and dissembled with hym in their tonges.
For their herte was not whole with him, neither continued they in his couenaunt.
But he was so mercifull, that he forgaue their misdedes, and destroyed them not. Yea, many a tyme turned he hys wrathe awaye, and wolde not suffre hys whole dyspleasure to aryse.
For he considered that they wer but flesh: euen a wynde that passeth awaye, and commeth not agayne.
O how ofte haue they greued hym in the wyldernesse? How many a tyme haue they prouoked hym in the deserte?
They turned backe, and tempted God, & moued the holy one in Israel.
They thought not of hys hand, in the day when he delyuered them from the hande of the enemye.
Howe he had wroughte hys myracles in Egypte, and hys wonders in the lande of Zoan.
How he turned their waters into bloude, so that they myghte not dryncke of the ryuers.
How he sent lyce among them, to eate them vp, and frogges to destroye them.
How he gaue their frutes vnto the catyrpyller, & their labour vnto the greshopper.
How he bete doune theyr vyneyardes wt hayle stones, and their molbery trees wyth the frost.
How he smote theyr cattel with haylestones, & their flockes with hote thonder boltes.
How he sent vppon them the furiousnesse of his wrath, anger & displeasure: with trouble and falling in of euell aungels.
When he made a waye to hys fearful indignacion, and spared not their soules from death, yea, & gaue their cattell ouer to the pestilence.
When he smote al the first born in Egipt, the mooste principall and mightyest in the dwellynges of Ham.
But as for his owne people, he lead them forth lyke shepe, and caried them in the wyldernesse lyke a flocke.
He brought them out safely, that they shoulde not feare, and ouerwhelmed their enemyes with the sea.
He caryed them vnto the borders of his Sanctuary: euen into thys hyl, which he purchased with hys ryghthande.
He dyd cast out the Heathen before them, caused their lande to be deuyded among them for an heritage, and made the trybes of Israel to dwell in their tentes.
For all this they tempted & displeased the most hye God, and kept not hys couenaunt.
But turned their backes, and fell awaye lyke their forefathers, startynge asyde like a broken boowe.
And so they greued hym with theyr hye places, & prouoked him with their ymages.
When God hearde thys, he was wroth, and toke sore dyspleasure at Israell.
So that he forsoke the Tabernacle in Silo, euen his habitacyon wherin he dwelte amonge men.
He delyuered their power into captyuitye and their glory into the enemies hande.
He gaue his people ouer into the swearde for he was wroth wyth hys herytage.
The fyre consumed their yonge men, and their maydens were not geuen to mariage.
Their Prestes were slaine with the swerd and there were no wyddowes to make lamentacyon.
So the Lorde, awaked as one oute of slepe, and lyke a gyaunte refreshed wyth wyne.
He smote hys enemyes in the hynder partes, and put them to perpetuall shame.
He refused the tabernacle of Ioseph, and chose not the trybe of Ephraim.
Neuertheles, he chose the trybe of Iuda, euen the hyll of Syon which he loued.
And there he buylded hys temple on hye, and layd the foundation of it like the ground that it myght perpetually endure.
He chose Dauid also hys seruaunte, and toke hym away from the shepe foldes.
As he was folowynge the yewes greate with yonge, he toke him, that he myghte fede Iacob hys people, & Israel hys enherytance.
So he fedde them wyth a fayethfull and true herte, and ruled them wyth diligence of of his power.
79: A Psalme of Asaph. O God, the Heathen are fallen into thyne heritage: the holy temple haue they defiled, and made Ierusalem an heape of stones.
The deade bodye of thy seruauntes haue they geuen vnto the foules of the ayre to be deuoured, and the flesh of thy saintes vnto the beastes of the lande.
Their bloude haue they shed lyke water on euery syde of Ierusalem, and ther was no man to bury them.
We are become an open shame vnto oure enemyes, a verye scorne and derysyon vnto them that are rounde aboute vs.
Lorde, howe longe wylt thou be angrye? shall thy ielousy burne lyke fyre for euer?
Poure oute thyne indignacyon vpon the Heathen that knowe the not, and vpon the Kyngdomes that call not vpon thy name.
For they haue deuoured Iacob, and laied wast his dwellynge place.
O remembre not oure olde synnes, but haue mercye vpon vs, and that soone, for we are come to greate mysery.
Helpe, vs, O God oure sauyoure, for the glory of thy name: O deliuer vs, and forgeue vs oure synnes for thy names sake.
Wherfore shall the Heathen say: wher is now their God? O lette the vengeaunce of thy seruauntes bloude that is shed, be openly shewed vpon the Heathen in our syght.
O Let the sorowfull sighehyng of the presoners come before the, and accordinge vnto the power of thyne arme, preserue those that are appoynted to dye.
And for the blasphemye wherewyth oure neyghboures haue blasphemed the, rewarde them, O Lorde, seenu folde into theyr bosome.
So we that be the people and shepe of thy pasture, shall geue the thanckes for euer, and wyll all waye be shewynge forth thy prayse more and more.
80: To the chaunter, vpon Sosanim, a Psalme of Asaph. Heare O thou shepeherde of Israel, thou that leadest Iacob lyke a flocke of shepe: shew thy self, thou that sittest vppon the Cherubyns.
Before Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manasses: stirre vp thy power, & come help vs.
Turne vs agayn, O God, shew the light of thy countenaunce, and we shalbe whole.
O Lord God of hostes, howe longe wilt thou be angry ouer the praier of thy people?
Thou hast fed them with the bread of teares, yea, thou hast geuen them plenteousnes of teares to drynke.
Thou haste made vs a verye stryfe vnto oure neyghbours, and oure enemyes laugh vs to scorne.
Turne vs agayne, thou God of hoostes, shewe the light of thy countenaunce, & we shalbe whole.
Thou hast broughte a vyneyarde oute of Egypte, thou diddest cast out the Heathen, & planted it.
Thou madest rowme for it, and caused it to take rote, so that it fylled the lande.
The hylles were couered with the shadow of it, and so were the stronge Cedre trees wt the bowes therof.
She stretched out her braunches vnto the sea, and her bowes vnto the water.
Why haste thou then broken doune her hedge, that all they whiche go by, plucke of her grapes?
Then wylde bore out of the wood hath roted it vp, and the beastes of the felde haue deuoured it.
Turne the agayne, thou God of hoostes, loke doune from heauen, beholde and vyset this vyneyarde.
Maynteyne it, that thy rightehande hath planted, and the sonne whom thou madest so muche of for thy self.
For why? it is brent with fyre, and lyeth waste: O let them peryshe at the rebuke of thy wrath.
Let thy hande be vpon the man of thy right hande, and vpon the man whome thou madest so much of for thyne owne selfe.
And so will not we go back from the: Oh let vs lyue, & we shall call vpon thy name.
Turne vs agayne, O Lorde God of hoostes, shewe the light of thy countenaunce, & we shalbe whole.
81: To the chaunter vpon Githith, of Asaph. Singe merely vnto God which is our strengthe, make a chearfull noyse vnto the god of Iacob.
Take the Psalme, brynge hyther the tabret, the mery harpe & lute.
Blowe vp the trompettes in the new mone, vpon our solempne feast daye.
For this is the vse in Israel, and a lawe of the God of Iacob.
This he ordeined in Ioseph for a testimony, when he came out of Epipt, & had heard a straunge language.
When he eased hys shoulder from the burthen, and when hys handes were deliuered from the pottes.
When thou callest vpon me in trouble, I helped the, and hearde the, what tyme as the storme fell vpon the, I proued the also at the water of stryfe. Selah.
Heare, O my people, for I assure the O Israel, if thou wilt herken vnto me:
There shal no straunge God be in the, neither shalt thou worshippe any other God.
I am the Lord thy God, which broughte the out of the lande of Egipt, open thy mouth wyde, and I shall fyll it.
But my people wolde not heare my voice and Israel wolde not obey me.
So I gaue them vp vnto their owne hertes luste, and let them folowe theyr owne ymaginacions.
O that my people wolde obeye me, for if Israel wolde walke in my wayes:
I should soone put doune their enemyes, and turne myne hande againste their aduersaries.
The haters of the Lord should mysse Israel, but their tyme shoulde endure for euer.
He should feade them with the finest wheat floure, and satisfye them with hony out of the stony rocke.
82: A Psalme of Asaph. God standeth in the congregacion of the Goddes, and is a iudge amonge the iudges.
How long will ye geue wrong iudgement, and accept the personnes of the vngodly? Selah.
Defende the poore and fatherlesse, se that suche as be in nede & necessitie haue right.
Deliuer the outcaste & poore, & saue hym from the hande of the vngodly.
Neuerthelesse, they will not be learned & vnderstande, but walke on styll in darkenesse: therfore must all the foundacions of the lande be moued.
I haue sayde: ye are Goddes, ye all are the chyldren of the moost hyest.
But ye shall dye lyke men, and fall lyke one of the tyrauntes.
Aryse, O God, & iudge thou the earth, for all the Heathen are thyne by enheritaunce.
83: A songe and Psalme of Asaph. Holde not thy tongue, O God, kepe not styll silence, refrayne not thy self O God.
For lo, thyne enemies make a murmurynge, and they that hate the, lyft vp their heade.
They ymagyn craftely agaynst thy people, and take counsayll agaynste thy secrete ones.
Come (saye they) let vs rote them out from amonge the people, that the name of Israell maye be put out of remembraunce.
For they haue caste their heades together with one consent, & are confederate agaynst the.
The tabernacles of the Edomites and Ismaelytes, the Moabytes and Hagarenes.
Gebal, Ammom, and Amalech: the Philistines with them that dwell at Tyre.
Assur also is ioyned vnto them, and helpe the chyldren of Loth. Selah.
But do thou to them as vnto the Madianites, vnto Sisera, and vnto Iabin by the broke of Kyson.
Whych peryshed at Endor, & became as the donge of the earth.
Make their prynces lyke Oreb & Zeb. Yea, make all their prynces lyke as Zebea & Salmana.
Whiche saye: we will haue the houses of God in possession.
O my God, make them lyke vnto a whele, and as the stubble before the wynde.
Lyke as a fyre that burneth vp the wood, and as the flame that consumeth the mountaynes.
Persecute them euen so with thy tempest, and make them afrayed with thy storme.
Make their faces ashamed, O Lord that they maye seke thy name.
Let them be confounded and vexed euer more and more: let them be put to shame and perishe.
That they may know that thou art alone that thy name is the Lorde, & that thou onely art the moost hyest ouer all the earth.
84: Vpon Githith, a Psalm of the sonnes of Corah. O howe amiable are thy dwellinges, thou Lord of hoostes?
My soule hath a desyre & longing for the court of the Lord, my hert and my fleshe reioyse in the lyuyng God.
For the sparow hath founde her an house and the swalow a nest, where she maye laye her yonge: euen thy aulters O Lorde of hostes, my kynge and my God.
O how blessed are they that dwell in thy house, they are all way praysing the. Selah.
Blessed are the men whose strengthe is in the, in whose herte are thy wayes.
Which goinge thorow the vale of misery vse it for a well, and the poles are filled with water.
They go from strength to strength, and so the God of Goddes appeareth vnto them in Sion.
O Lord God of hostes, heare my prayer: herken O God of Iacob.
Beholde O God our defence, loke vpon the face of thyne anoynted.
For one daye in thy courte is better then a thousande. I had rather be a dore keper in the house of my God, then to dwell in the tentes of the vngodly.
For the Lord God is a light and defence, the Lorde wyll geue grace and worshyppe, and no good thynge shall he wytholde from them that lyue a godly lyfe.
O Lorde God of Hostes, blessed is the man that putteth his truste in the.
85: To the chaunter, a Psalme of the sonnes of Corah. Lorde, thou barest a loue vnto thy land thou dydest brynge agayne the captyuyte of Iacob.
Thou dydest forgeue the offence of thy people, and couerdest al their synnes. Sela.
Thou takest away al thy displeasure, and turnedest thy selfe from thy wrathfull indignacyon.
Turne vs then. O God oure Sauyoure, and let thyne anger ceasse from vs.
Wylt thou be dyspleased at vs for euer? wylt thou stretch out thy wrath from one generacyon to another?
Wylt thou not turne agayne and quycken vs, that thy people maye reioyse in the?
I wyll herken what the Lorde God wyll saye for he shall speake peace vnto hys people and to hys saynctes, that they turne not them selues vnto folyshnes.
For hys saluacyon is nye them that feare hym so, that glory shall dwell in oure lande.
Mercy and trueth are met together, ryghtuousnesse and peace kysseth eche other.
Trueth shall ryse oute of the earthe, and ryghtuousnesse shal loke downe from heauen
And why? the Lorde shall shewe louynge kyndnesse, and oure lande shal geue her encrease.
Rightuousnes shall go before hym, and prepare the waye for his commynge.
86: A prayer of Dauyd. Bow downe thine eare, O Lord and heare me, for I am comfortles and poore.
O kepe my soule, for I am holy my God, helpe thy seruante that putteth his trust in the.
Be merciful vnto me, O Lord, for I cal dayly vpon the.
Comfort the soule of thy seruaunt, for vnto the, O Lord, do I lyft vp my soule.
For thou Lorde arte good and gracyous, and of greate mercye vnto all them that call vpon the.
Geue eare Lord vnto my praier, and ponder my humble desyre.
In the tyme of my trouble I cal vpon the, for thou hearest me.
Amonge the Goddes ther is none like vnto the, O Lorde, there is not one that can do as thou doest.
All nacyons whom thou hast made, shall come and worship before the, O Lorde, and shal gloryfy thy name.
For thou art great, thou dost wonderous thinges, thou art God alone.
Leade me in thy way, O Lord, that I may walke in thy trueth: O let my herte delyte in fearyng thy name.
I thanke the. O Lorde my God, and will prayse thy name for euer.
For great is thy mercy towarde me, thou hast delyuered my soule from the nether most hell.
O God the proude are rysen agaynst me, and the congregacyon of the myghtye seketh after my soule, and sette not the before theyr eyes.
But thou, O Lord God, art ful of compassion, and mercy, long suffring, great in goodnes and truth.
O turne the then vnto me, haue mercy vpon me: geue thy strength vnto thy seruante, and helpe the sonne of thyne handmayde.
Shew some token vpon me for good, that they which hate me, maye se it, and be ashamed: because thou Lord hast helped me, and comforted me.
87: A Psalme and songe of the sonnes of Corah Her foundatyons are vpon the holye hylles:
the Lorde loueth the gates of Syon more then all the dwellynges, of Iacob.
Very excellent thynges are spoken of the thou cyty of God. Selah.
I wyll thynke vpon Rahab and Babilon so that they shall know me. Yea the Philistines also, and they of Tire wyth the Morians. Lo ther was he borne.
And of Sion it shalbe reported, that he was borne in her, euen the most hyest whych hath buylded her.
The Lorde shall cause it to be preached & wrytten amonge the people, that he was borne ther. Selah.
Therfore the dwellynge of all syngers & daunsers is in the.
88: A Psalme and songe, of the sonnes of Corah, to the chaunter vpon Mahelath, for affliccyon, an instruccyon of Heman the Ezrathyte. O Lord God my sauiour, I cry day and nyghte before the:
Oh let my praier enter into thy presence, incline thyne eare vnto my callynge.
For my soule is full of trouble, and my lyfe draweth nye vnto hell.
I am counted as one of them that go downe vnto the pitte, I am euen as a man that hath no strength.
Fre among the dead, like vnto them that lye in the graue, whyche be out of remembraunce, and are cutte away from thy hand.
Thou hast layed me, in the lowest pytte, in the darcknesse and in the depe.
Thyne indignacion lieth harde vpon me, and thou vexest me wyth all thy floudes Selah.
Thou hast put awaye myn acquaintance farre fro me, and made me to be abhorred of them: I am so faste in pryson, that I can not get forth.
My syght fayleth for very trouble: Lord I call dayly vpon the, and stretch oute myne handes vnto the.
Doest thou shewe wonders amonge the deade? Can the Phisicions raise them vp againe that they maye prayse the?
Maye thy louynge kyndnes be shewed in the graue or thy faythfulnesse in destruccyon:
May thy wonderous workes be knowne in the darcke, or thy ryghtuousnes in the land wher al thinges are forgotten?
Vnto the I crye, O Lorde, and early commeth my prayer before the.
Lorde, why putteste thou awaye my soule? Wherfore hydest thou thy face fro me?
My strength is gone for very sorow & myserye, wyh fearfulnesse do I beare thy burthens.
Thy wrathfull dyspleasure goeth ouer me the feare of the, oppresseth me.
They come rounde about me dayly lyke water, and compasse me together on euerye side.
My louers, and frendes hast thou put awaye fro me, and turned awaye myne acquayntaunce.
89: An instruccyon yf Ethan the Ezrahyte. My songe shalbe alway of the louynge kyndnesse of the Lorde, wyth my mouth wyl I euer be shewynge thy faythfulnes from one generacyon to another.
For I haue sayed, mercy shalbe set vp for euer, thy faythfulnesse shalt thou stablysh in the heauens.
I haue made a couenaunt wyth my chosen, I haue sworne vnto Dauid my seruant.
Thy sede wyll I stablyshe for euer, and set vp thy trone from one generacyon to another Selah.
O Lorde the verye heauens shall prayse thy wonderous, worckes, yea and thy faythfulnes in the congregation of the saynctes.
For who is he amonge the cloudes, that may be compared vnto the Lord. Yea, what is he among the Gods that is like vnto the lord?
God is greatly to be feared in the councel of the saintes and to be had in reuerence of al them that are aboute hym.
O Lorde God of Hostes who is lyke vnto the in power? thy trueth is round about the
Thou rulest the pryde of the sea, thou stillest the waues therof, when they aryse.
Thou breakest the proude, like one that is wounded, thou scatrest thine enemies abroad with thy mightye arme.
The heauens are thine, the earth is thine: thou hast layed the foundation of the rounde world, and al that therin is.
Thou hast made the north and the south, Tabor and Hermon shal reioyse in thy name
Thou hast a myghty arme, stronge is thy hande, and hye is thy righthande.
Righteousnes and equite is the habitacion of thy seate, mercy and truethe go before thy face.
Blessed is the people, O Lorde, that can reioyse in the, & walketh in the lyghte of thy countenauce.
Their delyte is in thy name all the daye longe, and thorowe thy righteousnesse they shalbe exalted.
For thou art the glory of their strength, & thorow thy fauoure shalt thou lyfte vp oure hornes.
The Lorde is our defence, and the holy one of Israel is our kyng.
Thou spakest sometyme in visions vnto thy saynctes, and saydest: I haue layed helpe vpon one that is mighty, I haue exalted one chosen out of the people.
I haue founde Dauid my seruaunt, with my holy oyle haue I anoynted hym.
My hande shal holde him fast, and myne arme shall strengthen hym.
The enemye shall not ouercome hym, & the sonne of wyckednesse shall not hurte hym.
I shall smyte doune hys foes before hys face, and plage them that hate hym.
My trueth also & my mercy shalbe wyth hym, and in my name shall hys horne be exalted.
I will set hys hande in the sea, & his right hande in the floudes.
He shall call me, thou art my father, my God, and the strength of my saluacion.
And I will make hym my fyrste borne, hyer then the kynges of the earth.
My mercy wyll I kepe for hym for euermore, and my couenaunte shall stande faste with hym.
Hys sede wyll I make to endure for euer, yea, and his trone as the dayes of heauen.
But if hys chyldren forsake my law, and walke not in my iudgementes.
If they breake myne ordynaunces, & kepe not my commaundementes.
I will vyset their offences wyth the rodde, and their synnes wit scourges.
Neuerthelesse, my louinge kyndnesse wil I not vtterly take from hym, nor suffre my trueth to fayle.
My couenaunt wyl I not breake, nor disanulle the thynge that is gone out of my lippes.
I haue sworne once by my holinesse, that I will not fayle Dauid.
Hys sede shall endure for euer, and hys seate also lyke as the sunne before me.
He shall stande faste for euermore as the moone, and as the faythfull wytnesse in heauen. Selah.
But now thou forsakest & abhorrest thine anoynted, and art displeased at hym.
Thou hast turned backe the couenaunte of thy seruaunt, and caste hys croune to the grounde.
Thou hast ouerthrowen all his hedges, & broken doune his stronge holdes.
All they that go by, spoyle hym, he is become a rebuke vnto hys neyghbours.
Thou settest vp the righthande of his enemyes, and makest all hys aduersaries to reioyse.
Thou hast taken awaye the strengthe of his swerde, and geuest him not victory in the battayle.
Thou hast put out his glory, and cast his trone doune to the grounde.
The dayes of his youth hast thou shortened, & couered him with dishonoure. Selah.
Lord, how longe wilt thou hyde thy self? For euer? shall thy wrathe burne lyke fyre?
O remembre how shorte my time is, hast thou made all men for nought?
What man is he that lyueth, and shall not se death? Maye a man deliuer his owne soule from the hande of hell? Selah.
Lorde, where are thy olde louing kyndnesses, whyche thou sworest vnto Dauid in thy trueth?
Remembre Lord the rebuke that the multitude of the people do vnto thy seruauntes, and how I haue borne it in my bosome.
Wherwith thyne enemyes blaspheme the, and sclaunder the footesteppes of thyne anoynted.
Thankes be too the Lorde for euermore: Amen: Amen.
90: A prayer of Moyses the man of God. Lorde thou art oure refuge from one generacion to another.
Before the mountaines were broughte forthe, or euer the earthe and the worlde were made, thou art God from euerlastynge and worlde without ende.
Thou turnest man to destruccyon, Agayne, thou sayest: come agayne ye chyldren of men
For a thousande yeares in thy sighte are but as yesterdaye that is past, and lyke as it were a nyght watch.
As sone as thou scatrest them, they are euen as a slepe, & fade awaye sodenly like the grasse.
In the mornyng it is grene and groweth vp, but in the euenynge it is cut doune and wythered.
For we consume awaye in thy displeasure, and are afrayed at thy wrathful indignacion.
Thou settest our misdedes before the, and our secrete sinnes in the light of thy countenaunce.
For when thou art angrye, all oure dayes are gone, we brynge our yeares to an ende, as it were a tale that is tolde.

The dayes of oure age are .iij. score yeares and ten: and though men be so strong that they come to foure score yeares, yet is their strength then but laboure, & sorowe: so soone passeth it awaye, and we are gone.
But who regardeth the power of thy wrath thy fearfull and terrible displeasure?
O teach vs to numbre our daies, that we maye apply our hertes vnto wisdome.
Turne the agayn (O Lorde) at the last, & be gracious vnto thy seruauntes.
O satisfie vs with thy mercy, & that sone, so shall we reioyse and be glad all the dayes of our lyfe.
Comforte vs agayne, now after the tyme that thou hast plaged vs, and for the yeares wherin we haue suffred aduersitie.
Shewe thy seruauntes thy worke, & their chyldren thy glory.
And the glorious maiesty of the Lord our God be vpon vs: O prospere thou the worke of our handes vpon vs, O prospere thou our handy worke.
91: Who so dwelleth vnder the defence of the most hyest, & abydeth vnder the shadowe of the almightye.
He shal say vnto the Lorde: O my hope, and my strong holde, my God, in whome I will trust.
For he shall delyuer the from the snare of the hunter, and from the noysome pestylence.
He shall couer the vnder hys wynges, that thou mayest be safe vnder his fethers: his faythfulnesse & trueth shalbe thy shylde and buckler.
So that thou shalt not nede to be afrayed for any bugges by night, nor for the arrowe that flyeth by daye.
For the pestilence that crepeth in the darkenesse, nor for the sikenesse that destroyeth in the noone daye.
A thousande shall fall beside the, and ten thousande at thy righthande, but it shall not come nye the.
Yea, with thyne eyes shalt thou beholde, and se the rewarde of the vngodly.
For thou Lorde art my hope, thou hast set thyne house of defence very hye.
There shall no euell happen vnto the, neither shall any plage come nye thy dwelling.
For he shall gyue his aungels charge ouer the, to kepe the in all thy wayes.
They shall beare the in their handes, that thou hurt not thy fote agaynst a stone.
Thou shalt go vpon the Lyon and Adder the yonge lyon and the Dragon shalte thou treade vnder thy fete.
Because he hath set his loue vppon me, I shall deliuer hym: I shal defende him, for he hath knowen my name.
When he calleth vpon me, I shall heare hym: yea, I am with hym in hys trouble, wherout I will deliuer him, and bring hym to honoure.
With longe lyfe will I satisfye him, and shewe hym my saluacion.
92: A Psalme of the songe for the Sabboth daye. It is a good thynge too geue thankes vnto the Lord, and to synge prayses vnto thy name, O moost hyest.
To tell of thy louyng kyndnesse early in the mornyng. and of thy trueth in the night season.
Vpon an instrument of ten strynges, vpon the lute and with a songe vpon the harpe.
For thou lord hast made me glad thorow thy workes, and I will reioyse ouer the operacion of thy handes.
O Lorde, how glorious are thy workes, thy thoughtes are very depe.
An vnwyse man will not knowe thys, and a foole will not vnderstande it.
That the vngodly are grene as the grasse and that all the workes of wickednes do florish to be destroyed for euer.
But thou Lorde O mooste hyest, abydest worlde without ende.
For lo, thyne enemyes, O Lord, lo, thyne enemyes shall perishe, and all the workers of wickednes shalbe scatred abroade.
But my horne shalbe exalted like the horne of an Vnicorne, & shalbe anoynted wyth fresh oyle.
Myne eye also shall se hys luste of myne enemyes, and myne eare shall heare his desire of the wicked that ryse vp agaynst me.
The righteous shall florish lyke a palme tree, and growe like a Cedre of Libanus.
Suche as be planted in the house of the Lorde, be frutefull,
That they maye shew, how true the Lorde my strength is, and that there is no vnrighteousnesse in hym.
93: The Lorde is kyng, and hath put on glorious apparell, the Lorde hath put on his apparell, & gyrded him selfe with strengthe: he hath made the rounde world so sure, that it can not be moued.
From that tyme forth hath thy seate bene prepared, thou art from euerlastyng.
The floudes aryse (O Lorde) the floudes lyft vp their noyse, the floudes lyfte vp theyr waues.
The waues of the sea are mightye, & rage horribly: but yet the Lorde that dwelled on hye, is mightier.
Thy testimonies, O LORD, are very sure, holynesse becommeth thyne house for euer.
94: O Lorde God, to whome vengeaunce belongeth: thou God to whome vengeaunce belongeth shewe thy self.
Aryse thou iudge of the world & rewarde the proude after their deseruyng.
Lorde how longe shall the vngodly, how longe shall the vngodly triumphe?
How longe shall all wicked doers speake so disdaynfully, and make such proude boastynge?
They smyte doune thy people, O Lorde, and trouble thine heritage.
They murthur the wydowe & the straunger, and put the fatherlesse to death.
And yet they saye: Tushe, the Lorde seyth not, the God of Iacob regardeth it not.
Take hede, ye vnwyse among the people: O ye fooles, when will ye vnderstande?
He that planted the eare, shal he not heare? he that made the eye, shal not he se?
He that nurtureth the Heathen, and teacheth a man knowlege, shall not he punish?
The Lord knoweth the thoughtes of men, that they are but vayne.
Blessed is the man, whome thou learnest (O LORDE) and teacheste hym in thy lawe.
That thou mayest geue hym pacience in tyme of aduersitie, vntil the pytte be dygged vp for the vngodly.
For the Lorde will not fayle his people, neither will he forsake his inheritaunce.
And why? iudgement shalbe turned agayn vnto righteousnesse, and all suche as be true of hert shall folow it.
Who ryseth vp with me agaynst the wicked? who taketh my parte agaynste the euell doers?
If the Lord had not helped me, my soule had almost bene put to silence.
When I sayde: my fote hath slypped, thy mercy (O Lord) helde me vp.
In the multitude of the sorowes that I had in my herte, thy comfortes haue refreshed my soule.
Wilt thou haue any thing to do with the stoole of wickednesse, which ymagineth mischief in the lawe?
They gather them together agaynste the soule of the righteous, and condemne the innocent bloude.
But the Lord is my refuge, my God is the strength of my confidence.
He shall recompence them their wickednesse, & destroye them in their owne malyce: yea, the Lorde our God shall destroy them.
95: O come let vs prayse the Lord, let vs hertely reioyse in the strength of our saluacion.
Let vs come before his presence with thankesgeuynge, & shewe oure selfe gladde in hym with Psalmes.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great kyng aboue all Goddes.
In his hand are al the corners of the earth, and the strength of the hylles is his also.
The sea is his, for he made it, & his handes prepared the drye lande.
O come, let vs worshippe & bowe doune our selfes: Let vs knele before the Lord our maker.
For he is oure God: & we are the people of his pasture, and the shepe of his handes. To daye if ye wil heare his voyce,
harden not youre hertes, as when ye prouoked in tyme of temptacion in the wildernes.
Where your fathers tempted me, proued me, and sawe my workes.
.xl. yeares long was I greued with the generacion, & sayd: they euer erre in their hertes, they verely haue not knowen my wayes.
Therfore I sayd vnto them in my wrath, that they should not enter into my rest.
96: O synge vnto the Lorde a newe songe, singe vnto the Lorde all the whole earth.
Synge vnto the Lord, and prayse his name, be tellyng of his saluacion from daye to daye.
Declare his honour among the Heathen, and his wonders among all people.
For the Lord is great, and can not worthely be praysed: he is more to be feared then all goddes.
As for all the goddes of the Heathen, they be but Idols, but it is the Lorde that made the heauens.
Thankesgeuynge and worshippe are before hym, power & honoure are in hys Sanctuary.
Ascribe vnto the Lord (O ye kynredes of the Heathen) ascribe vnto the Lord worship and strength.
Ascribe vnto the Lord the honoure of his name, brynge presentes, and come into hys courte.
O worship the lorde in the beuty of holynesse, lette the whole earthe stande in awe of hym.
Tell it out amonge the Heathen, that the Lorde is kynge: and that it is he, which hath made the rounde worlde so faste, that it can not be moued, and howe that he shall iudge the people righteously.
Let the heauens reioyse, and let the earth be glad: let the sea make a noyse, yea, and all that therin is.
Let the felde be ioyfull and all that is in it, lette all the trees of the woode leape for ioye.
Before the lorde, for he commeth: for he commeth to iudge the earth: yea, with ryghteousnesse shall he iudge the worlde, and the people with his trueth.
97: The Lord is king, the earth may be glad therof: yea, the multitude of the Iles may be glad therof.
Cloudes & darkenesse are round about him, righteousnesse & iudgement are the habitacion of hys seate.
There goeth a fyre before hym, to burne vp hys enemyes on euery syde.
Hys lightenynges geue shyne vnto the worlde, the earth seyth it, and is afrayed.
The hilles melt like waxe at the presence of the lord of the whole earth.
The very heauens declare his righteousnes, and all the people se his glory.
Confounded be all thei that worship ymages, and delyte in their Idols: worship him all ye Goddes.
Sion heareth of it & reioyseth: yea, & all the daughters of Iuda are glad because of thy iudgementes, O lorde.
For thou lorde art the most hyest ouer all the earth, thou arte exalted farre aboue all goddes.
O ye that loue the lorde, se that ye hate that thyng whiche is euell: the lorde preserueth the soules of his saynctes, he shall deliuer them from the hande of the vngodly.
There is sprong vp a lighte for the ryghteous, and a ioyfull gladnesse for suche as be true herted.
Reioyse therfore in the lorde, ye ryghteous: and geue thankes for a remembraunce of hys holinesse.
98: A Psalme. O synge vnto the Lorde a new song, for he hath done maruelous thynges. With hys owne ryght hande and with his holy arme hathe he gotten the victory.
The lord hath declared his sauyng health & hys righteousnes hathe he openly shewed in the sight of the Heathen.
He hath remembred his mercy and trueth towarde the house of Israel: so that all the endes of the worlde, se the sauing health of our God.
Shewe youre selfes ioyfull vnto the Lorde all ye landes, synge, reioyse, and geue thanckes.
Prayse the Lordes, vpon the harpe, synge to the harpe wyth a psalme of thanckesgeuynge
With trompettes also and shawmes: O shewe youre selues ioyfull before the Lorde the kynge.
Let the sea make a noyse and all that therin is, yea the whole worlde, and al that dwel therein.
Let the floudes clappe their handes, and let al the hylles be ioyful together.
Before the Lorde, for he is come to iudge the earth. Yea wyth ryghtuousnes shall he iudg the worlde, and the people wyth equyte.
99: The Lorde is kynge, be the people neuer so vnpaciente: he sytteth vpon the Cherubyns, be the earth neuer so vnquiete.
The Lord is greate in Sion, & hye aboue all people.
O let men geue thanckes vnto thy greate and wonderfull name, for it is holye.
The kinges power loueth iudgment, thou preparest equite, thou executest iudgment and ryghtuousnes in, Iacob.
O magnyfy the Lorde oure God, fal down before his fote stole, for he is holye.
Moyses ond Aaron amonge hys pryestes and Samuell amonge such as call vpon hys name: these called vpon the Lorde, and he hearde them.
He spake vnto them out of the cloudy piller for he kepte hys testymonyes, and the lawe that gaue them.
Thou heardest them, O Lorde oure God thou forgauest them O God, and punyshedst their owne inueucions.
O magnyfye the Lorde oure God, and worshyppe hym vpon hys holy hyll, for the Lorde oure God is holy.
100: A Psalme of praise. O be ioiful in God (al ye landes)
serue the Lorde with gladnes, come before his presence wyth ioye.
Be ye sure, that the Lord he is God: It is he that hath made vs, and not we our selues: we are but his people, and the shepe of his pastoure.
O go youre waye into hys gates then with thanckesgeuynge, and into his courtes with prayse, be thanckefull vnto hym, and speake good of his name.
For the Lorde is gracyous, hys mercie is euerlastynge, and hys trueth endureth from generatyon to generacyon.
101: A Psalme of Dauid. My songe shalbe of mercye and iudgment yea vnto the, O Lord wyll I synge.
O let me haue vnderstandynge in the way of Godlynesse vntyll the tyme that thou come vnto me: and so shall I walcke in my house wyth an innocent herte.
I wyl take no wycked thynge in hande, I hate the synne of vnfaythfulnesse, it shal not cleaue vnto me.
