A frowarde harte shall departe fro me I wyll not knowe a wicked personne.
Who so preuely sclaundereth hys neyghboure. hym wyl I destroye: Who so hath a prowd loke and an hye stomacke, I may not awaye with him.
Myne eyes shal loke for such as be faythfull in the lande, that they maye dwell wyth me: and who so leadeth a godly liue, shall be my seruaunt.
There shall no disceatfull personne dwell in my house he that telleth lyes shall not tary in my syght.
I shalll soone destroye all the vngodlie of the lande, that all wycked doers maye be roted out of the cytie of the Lord.
102: A prayer of the afflycte, when he was in woo, and powered oute hys complaynte before the Lord. Heare my prayer, O Lord, & and lette my crienge come vnto the.
Hyde not thy face fro me in the tyme of my trouble encline thyne eares vnto me when I call, O heare me, and that ryghte sone.
For my dayes are consumed awaye lyke smoke, and my bones are brent vp as it were a fyre brande.
My herte smytten doune and wythered lyke grasse, so that I forgette too eate my bread.
For the voyce of my gronynge, my bone wil scarse cleue to my flesh.
I am be come lyke a Pellicane in the wildernes, and lyke an owle in a broken wal.
I wake, and am euen as it were a sparow sittinge alone vpon the house toppe.
Myne enemyes reuyle me all the daye longe, they laugh me to scorne, & are sworne together agaynst me.
I eate ashes with my bread, and myngle my drynke with wepynge.
And that because of thyne indignacion & wrath, for thou hast taken me vp, and caste me awaye.
My dayes are gone lyke a shadowe, and I am wythered lyke grasse.
But thou O Lord, endurest for euer, and thy remembraunce thorow out all generacyons.
Aryse therfore & haue mercy vpon Sion, for it is time to haue mercy vpon her, yea, the tyme is come.
And why? thy seruauntes haue a loue too her stones, and it pitieth them to se her in the dust.
The Heathen shal feare thy name, O Lord, and all the kynges of the earth thy maiesty.
For the Lorde shall buylde vp Sion, and shall apeare in hys glory.
He turneth him vnto the prayer of the poore destitute, & despiseth not their desyre.
This shalbe wrytten for those that come after, that the people whiche shalbe borne, maye prayse the Lorde.
For he loketh doune from hys Sanctuary, out of the heauen doth the Lorde beholde the earth.
That he maye heare the mournynges of such as be in captiuitie, and deliuer the chyldren of death.
That they maye preache the name of the Lorde in Sion, and his worshippe at Hierusalem.
When the people are gathered together, & the kyngdomes also to serue the Lord.
He hath brought doune my strength in my iourney, and shortened my dayes.
Yet will I saye: O my God, take me not away in the myddest of myne age: as for thy yeares, they endure thorowe out all generacions.
Thou Lorde in the beginnyng hast layed the foundacion of the earth, and the heauens are the workes of thy handes.
They shal perish, but thou shalt endure: they all shall wexe olde as doth a garment, & as a vesture shalt thou chaunge them, & they shalbe chaunged.
But thou art the same, & thy yeares shall not fayle.
The chyldren of thy seruauntes shall continue, and their sede shall prospere in thy sighte.
103: Of Dauid. Prayse the Lorde O my soule: & all that is within me prayse hys holy name.
Prayse the Lord O my soule & forget not all his benefites.
Whych forgeueth all thy synnes, & healeth all thyne infirmities.
Which saueth thy lyfe from destruccion, and crouneth the with mercy, and louynge kyndnesse.
Whiche satisfeth thy desyre wyth good thynges, makyng the yonge and lusty as an Aegle.
The Lorde executeth righteousnesse and iudgement, for all theim that suffre wronge.
He shewed his wayes vnto Moses, & his workes vnto the chyldren of Israel.
The Lord is ful of compassion and mercy, long sufferyng, & of great goodnesse.
He will not alwaye be chydynge, neither will he kepe his anger for euer.
He hath not dealt with vs after oure sinnes, nor rewarded vs according to our wickednesse.
For loke how hye the heauen is in comparison of the earth, so greate is his mercy also towarde them that feare hym.
Loke how wyde the East is from the West, so farre hath he set oure sinnes from vs.
Yea, like as a father pitieth his owne children, euen so is the Lord mercifull vnto them that feare hym.
For he knoweth whereof we be made, he remembreth that we are but dust.
That a man in hys time is but as grasse, and florisheth as a floure of the felde.
For as sone, as the wynde goeth ouer it, it is gone, and the place thereof knoweth it no more.
But the mercyfull goodnesse of the Lorde endureth for euer and euer, vpon them that feare him, and his righteousnesse vpon their chyldren.
Suche as kepe hys couenaunte, & thynke vpon hys commaundementes to do them.
The Lorde hath prepared his seate in heauen, and his kingedome ruleth ouer all.
O prayse the Lorde ye aungels of his, ye that be myghty in strength fulfyllynge hys commaundement that men may here the voice of hys wordes.
O prayse the Lorde all ye his Hostes, yea seruauntes of his, that do hys pleasure.
O speake good of the Lorde al ye workes of his, in euery place of his dominion: praise thou the Lorde, O my soule.
104: Prayse the Lorde O my soule: O Lord my God, thou art become excedinge glorious, thou arte clothed with maiesty and honoure.
Thou deckest thy self with light, as it were with a garment, thou spredest out the heauen lyke a curtayne.
Thou voltest it aboue with waters, thou makest the cloudes thy charet, & goest vpon the wynges of the wynde.
Thou makest thyne aungels sprites, and thy ministers flammes of fyre.
Thou hast layed the earth vpon her foundacion, that it neuer moueth at any tyme.
Thou couerest it with the depe lyke as wt a garmente, so that the waters stande aboue the hylles.
But at thy rebuke they fle, at the voyce of thy thonder they are afrayed.
(Then are the hylles sene alofte, and the valleis beneth in their place which thou hast appoynted for them.)
Thou hast set them their boundes, which they maye not passe, that they turne not agayne to couer the earth.
Thou causest the welles to sprynge vp amonge the valleys, and the waters to runne amonge the hylles.
That all beastes of the felde maye haue drynke, & that the wilde asses maye quenche their thyrste.
Aboue vpon the hylles haue the foules of the ayre their habitacion, and singe amonge the braunches.
Thou waterest the hilles from aboue, the earth is filled wt the frutes of thy workes.
Thou bringest forth grasse for the cattell, and grene herbes for the seruice of men. Thou bringest fode out of the earth:
wyne to make glad the herte of man, oyle to make hym a chearfull countenaunce and bread to strength mans herte.
The trees of the Lord are ful of sappe, euen the trees of Libamis whiche he hathe planted.
There make the byrdes their nestes, & the fyrre hylles are a dwellyng for the storke.
The hilles are a refuge for the wilde goates, & so are the stony rockes for the conyes.
Thou hast appoynted the moone for certayne seasons, the sunne knoweth hys going doune.
Thou makest darkenesse, that it maye be night, wherin all the beastes of the forest do moue.
Yea, and the yonge lyons which roare after their praye, and seke their meate at God.
But when the sunne aryseth, they get them awaye together, and lye them doune in their dennes.
Then goeth man forth to hys worke, and to tyll hys lande vntyll the euenynge.
O Lord, how manifolde are thy workes, right wisely hast thou made them al: yea, the earth is full of thy ryches.
So is this great & wyde sea also, wherein are thynges creping innumerable, both smal and great beastes.
There go the shippes ouer, and there is the Leuiathan, whom thou hast made, to take hys pastyme therein.
They wayte all vpon the, that thou mayest geue them meate in due season.
When thou geuest it them, they gather it: when thou openest thyne hande, they are filled with good.
But when thou hydest thy face, they are sorowfull: if thou takest awaye their breth, they dye, & are turned agayne to their dust.
Agayne, when thou lettest thy brethe goo forth, they are made, and so thou renuest the face of the earth.
The glorious maiesty of the Lorde endureth for euer, & the Lorde reioyseth in hys workes.
The earth trembleth at the loke of hym, he doethe but touche the hylles and they smoke.
I wyll synge vnto the Lorde as longe as I lyue, I will prayse my God whyle I haue my beyng.
O that my wordes might please hym, for my ioye is in the Lorde.
As for synners, they shalbe consumed out of the earth, and the vngodlye shall come to an ende: but prayse thou the Lorde, O my soule. Prayse the euerlastynge.
105: O geue thankes vnto the Lord, and cal vpon his name: tel the people what thynges he hath done.
O let your songes be of him prayse hym, and let your talking be of al hys wonderous workes.
Gyue hys holye name a good report lette their hertes reioyse that seke the Lord.
Seke the Lord, and his strength, seke his face euermore.
Remember the maruelous worckes that he hath done, his wonders and the iudgementes of his mouth.
O ye sede of Abraham hys seruaunte, ye chyldren of Iacob hys chosen.
He is the Lorde oure God, whose punishmentes are thorow oute all the worlde.
He is alwaye myndeful of his couenaunt and promyse that he made to a thousand generations.
Yea the couenant that he made with Abraham, and the oth that, he sware vnto Isaac,
And appoynted the same vnto Iacob for a lawe, and to Israell for an euerlastynge testamente.
Sayenge: vnto the wyl I geue the land of Canaan, the lot of your heritage.
When there was yet but a fewe of them, and the straungers therin.
What tyme as they wente from one nacyon to another, from one kyngedome to another.
He suffered no man to hurt them, but reproued euen kynges for their sakes.
Touch not myne anoynted, do my prophetes no harme.
Moreouer he called for a dearth vpon the lande, and destroyed all the prouysyon of breade.
But he had sente a man before them, euen Ioseph whiche was solde to be a bonde seruaunte.
They hurte hys fete in the stockes the yron pearsed hys hert.
Vntill the tyme that his worde, and tyll the word of the Lorde had tryed hym.
Then sent the kyng & caused him to be deliuered, the prince of the people bad let him go
He made him Lorde of hys house, and ruler of all hys substaunce.
That he might enfourme his princes after hys wyl, & teach his Senatoures wisedom.
Israell also came into Egipte, and Iacob was a straunger in the lande of Ham.
But he increased hys people exceadyngly and made them stronger then their enemyes.
Whose hert turned so that they hated his people: and dealt vntruly wt hys seruauntes.
Then sente he Moses his seruaunte, and Aaron, whome he had chosen.
These dyd his tokens amonge them, and wonders in the lande of Ham.
He sente darcknesse and it was darcke, for they were not obedyent vnto hys worde.
He turned their waters into bloude, and slew theyr fysh.
Their land brought forth frogges, yea euen in their kynges chambers.
He spake the worde, and their came all maner of flyes and lyce in al their quarter
He gaue them hayle stones for rayne, and flammes of fyre in their land.
He smot their vineyeardes & figge trees, & destroyed the trees that were in their coastes.
He spake the worde, and ther were greshoppers and catyrpyllers innumerable.
These eate vp all the grasse in their land, and deuoured their frutes of the grounde.
He smote al the fyrst borne in the lande, euen the chefe of al their substaunce.
He broughte them forth wyth syluer and gold, ther was not one feble person amonge theyr trybes.
Egypte was glad of their departinge, for they were afrayed of them.
He spred out a cloude to be a couerynge, and fyres to geue lyght in the nyght season.
At their desyre, ther came quailes, and he fylled them wyth the breade of heauen.
He opened the rocke of stone, and the waters flowed out: so that ryuers ranne in the wyldernesse.
For why? he remembred his holy promes whyche he had made vnto Abraham his seruaunte.
Thus he broughte forth hys people wyth ioy, and his chosen with gladnesse.
And gaue them the landes of Heathen, where they toke the laboures of the people in possessyon.
That they myghte kepe hys statutes, and obserue his lawes. Prayse the euerlastynge.
106: Prayse the euerlastynge. O geue thankes vnto the Lorde, for he is gracyous, and hys mercy endureth for euer.
Who can expresse the noble actes of the Lord, or shewe forth al hys prayse?
Blessed are they that allwaye kepe iudgement, and do ryghtuousnes.
Remember vs, O Lorde, accordynge to the fauour that thou bearest vnto thy people O vyset vs wyth thy sauynge health.
That we myght se the pleasure of thy chosen, that we myght reioyse in the gladnesse of thy people, and geue thanckes with thine enherytaunce.
We haue synned wyth oure fathers, we haue done amysse, we haue dealt wyckedlye.
Oure fathers regarded not thy wonders in Egypte, they kepte not thy great goodnes in remembraunce: but were dysobedyent at the sea, euen at the reed sea.
Neuertheles, he helped them for hys names sake, that he myghte make hys power to be knowne.
He rebuked the read sea, and it was dryed vp: so he led them thorowe the depe as in a wyldernes.
Thus he saued them from the hand of the hater, and delyuered them from the hande of the enemye.
As for those that troubled them the waters ouerwhelmed them, ther was not one of them left.
Then beleued they in his worde, and sang prayse vnto hym.
But within a whyle they forgat his workes, and wold not abyde his councel.
A lust came vpon them in the wildernesse, so that they tempted God in the deserte.
Yet he gaue them their desire, and sent them ynough at their wylles.
They angred Moyses in the tentes, & Aaron the saynct of the Lord.
So the earth opened & swalowed vp Dathan, & couered the congregatyon of Abyram.
The fyre was kyndled in their companie, the flamme brent vp the vngodly.
They made a calfe in Horeb, and worshipped the molten ymage.
Thus they turned their glorye into the similitude of a calfe, that eateth hay.
They forgat God their Sauiour, whyche had done so greate thynges in Egypte.
Wonderous workes in the land of Ham and fearful thynges in the read sea.
So he sayde he wuld haue destroyed them had not Moses hys chosen stand before him in that gappe: to turne awaye his wrathfull indignatyon, lest he should destroy them.
Yea, they thought scorne of that pleasaunt lande, and gaue no credence vnto hys worde
But murmured in their tentes, and herkened not vnto the voyce of the Lord.
Then lyft he vp his hand against them to ouerthrowe them in the wildernes.
To cast out their sede among the nacions. and to scatter them in the landes.
They ioyned them selues vnto Baal Peor and eate the offeringes of the dead.
Thus they prouoked him vnto anger with their owne inuencyons, and the plage was great among them.
Then stode vp Phynehes and executed iustice, and so the plage ceased.
And that was counted vnto him for ryghtuousnesse, amonge all posterityes for euermore.
They angeryd hym also at the waters of strife, so that Moyses was punished for ther sakes.
Because they prouoked his spirite, and he told them plainly with his lippes.
Nether destroied they the Heathen, as the Lorde commaunded them.
But were mingled among the Heathen, and lerned their workes.
In so much that they worshipped their images, which turned to their owne decay.
Yea they offred their sons and their daughters vnto deuels.
And shed the innocent bloud of their sonnes and of their daughters, whom they offered vnto the ymages of Canaan, so that the land was defiled with bloud.
Thus were they stayned with their owne workes, and went a whoring with their owne inuencyons.
Therfore was the wrath of the Lord kindled agaynst hys people, in so much that he abhorred his owne enheritaunce.
And gaue them ouer into the hand of the Heathen, and they that hated them, were lordes ouer them.
Their enemyes oppressed them, and had them in subieccion.
Many a tyme did he delyuer them but they prouoked him wyth theyr owne inuencyons and were broughte downe for theyr wyckednesse.
Neuertheles when he saw their aduersitie he herd their complaynt.
He thought vpon hys couenaunt, and pytyed them, accordyng vnto the multytude of hys mercyes.
Yea he made all those that had led them awaye captyue, to pitiye them.
Delyuer vs, O Lorde oure God, and gather vs from amonge the Heathen: that we maye geue thanckes to thy holye name, and make our boast of thy prayse.
Blessed be the Lorde God of Israel from euerlastyng and world without ende, and let all people saye: Amen, Amen. Prayse the euerlastynge.
107: O geue thankes vnto the Lord, for he is gracious, & his mercy endureth for euer.
Let them geue thankes whome the Lord hath redemed, & deliuered from the hande of the enemye.
And gathered them out of the landes, from the East, from the West, from the North and from the South.
They went astraye in the wildernesse in an vntroden waye, and founde no cytye too dwell in.
Hungry & thirsty, and their soule faynted in them.
So they cryed vnto the Lorde in theyr trouble, and he deliuered them from theyr distresse.
He ledde them forth by the ryghte waye, that they myghte go to the cytye where they dwelt.
O that men wolde praise the goodnesse of the Lorde, and the wonders that he doth for the chyldren of men.
For he satisfied the empty soule, & fylled the hungry soule with good.
Such as sat in darkenesse and in the shadow of death, beyng fast bounde in mysery and yron.
Because they were not obedient to the commaundementes of God, but lightely regarded the counsayll of the moost hyghest.
Their hert was vexed with labour, they fel doune, and there was none to helpe them.
So they cryed vnto the LORD in their trouble, and he deliuered them oute of theyr dystresse.
He brought them out of darkenesse & oute of the shadow of death, & brake their bondes in sonder.
O that men wolde prayse the goodnesse of the Lord, and the wonders that he doth for the chyldren of men.
For he hath broken the gates of brasse, and smytten the barres of yron in sonder.
Folysh men were plaged for their offence and because of their wickednesse.
Their soule abhorred all maner of meate, they were euen harde at deaths dore.
So they cryed vnto the Lorde in their trouble, and he deliuered them oute of theyr distresse.
He sent hys worde and healed them, and saued them from destruccion.
O that men woulde prayse the goodnesse of the Lord, and the wonders that he doth for the chyldren of men.
That they wolde offre vnto him the sacrifice of thankesgeuyng, & tell out hys workes with gladnes.
They that go doune to the sea in shippes, and occupy their businesse in great waters.
These men se the workes of the Lorde, & his wonders in the deape.
For at his worde, the stormy winde aryseth, and lifteth vp the waues therof.
They are caryed vp to the heauen, & doun agayne too the deape, their soule melteth awaye in the trouble.
They rele to and fro, they stacker lyke a droncken man, and are at their wittes ende.
So they crye vnto the Lorde in their trouble, and he delyuereth them oute of their distresse.
He maketh the storme to ceasse, so that the waues are styll.
Then are they glad because they be at rest & so he bringeth them vnto the hauen, where they wolde be.
O that men wolde prayse the goodnes of the Lorde, and the wondres that he doth for the chyldren of men.
That they wolde exalte him in the congregacion of the people, & loane hym in the seate of the elders.
Which turneth the floudes into drye land, and drieth vp the water sprynges.
A frutefull lande maketh he baren, for the wickednesse of them that dwell therin.
Agayn, he maketh the wildernes a standinge water, and water springes of a drye grounde.
There he setteth the hongrye, that they maye buylde them a cytye to dwell in.
That they may sow their grounde, plante vyneyardes, to yelde them frutes of increase.
He blesseth them, so that they multiplye excedingly, and suffreth not their cattel to decrease.
When they are minished & brought lowe thorowe oppression, thorowe any plage or trouble.
Though he suffre them to be euell intreated thorow tyrauntes, or lette them wandre out of the waye in the wildernesse.
Yet helpeth he the poore out of misery (at the last) and maket hym an housholde lyke a flocke of shepe.
The righteous will considre this & reioyse, the mouth of all wyckednesse shalbe stopped.
Who so is wyse, & pondreth these thynges well, shal vnderstande the louyng kyndnesses of the Lorde.
108: A songe of Psalme of Dauid. O God, my herte is ready to synge, and to geue prayse. Awake, O my glorye,
awake lute and harpe, I my selfe wyll awake ryght early.
I wyll geue thanckes vnto the, O Lord, amonge the people. I wil syng prayses vnto the among the Heathen.
For the greatenesse of thy mercy is higher then the heauens, and thy faithfulnesse reacheth vnto the cloudes.
Set vp thy selfe, O God, aboue the heauens, and thy glory aboue al the eartth.
That thy beloued may be delyuered: helpe them with thy right hand and heare me
God hath spoken in his Sanctuary, whych thyng reioyseth me. I wyll deuyde Sichem, and meate out the valley of Suchoth.
Galaad is myne, Manasses is myne, Ephraym is the strength of my head, Iuda is my captaine.
Moab is my washpotte, ouer Edom will I stretch oute my shue, Phylystea shall be glad of me.
Who wyll lead me into the stronge cyty? Who wyll brynge me into Edom?
Shalt not thou do it (O God) which hast cast vs: out thou God, that wentest not forth with our Hostes?
O be thou our helpe in trouble, for vayne is the helpe of man.
Thorow God we shal do great actes, for it is he that shal treade downe our enemyes.
109: To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauyd. Holde not thy tong: O God of my praise.
For the mouth of the vngodlye yea and the mouth of the disceatfull is opened vpon me, and speake agaynste me wyth false tonges.
They compase me aboute with wordes of hatred, and fight against me without a cause
For the loue that I had vnto them, they take now my contrary parte, but I geue my selfe vnto prayer.
Thus they reward me euel for good, and hatred for my god wyll.
Set an vngodly man to be ruler ouer him and let Satan stande at his ryghte hande.
When sentence is geuen vpon him, let him be condempned, and let his prayer be turned into synne.
Let his daies be few, and his bishopricke let another take.
Let hys chyldren be fatherlesse, and hys wyfe a wydowe.
Let his children be vagabaundes, and bege their breade: lette them seke it, as they that be destroyed.
Let the extorcioner consume al that he hath and let straungers spoyle his laboure.
Let ther be no man to pytye, ner to haue compassyon vpon his fatherles chyldren.
Let hys ende be destruccyon, & in the next generacion let his name be cleane put oute.
Let the wickednesse of his fathers be had in remembraunce in the syght of the Lorde & and let not the synne of hys mother be done awaye.
Let them alway be before the Lorde, but as for the memoryall of them selues, let it perysh from out of the earth.
And that because hys mynde was not to do good. but persecuted the poore helplesse, and hym that was vexed at the harte, to slay hym.
Hys delyte was in cursynge, and therfore shall it happen vnto hym: he loued not blessynge and that shall be far from hym.
He clothed hym selfe wyth cursynge lyke as wyth a rayment: yea it wente into hys bowels lyke water, and lyke oile into his bone
Let it be vnto hym as the cloke that he hath vpon hym, and as the gyrdle that he is gyrded with al.
Let it thus happen from the Lorde vnto myne enemyes, and to those that speake euel agaynst my soule.
But deale thou wyth me, O Lorde God, accordynge vnto thy name, for swete is thy mercy. O deliuer me,
for I am helplesse, and pore and my herte is wounded within me.
I go hence lyke the shadowe that departeth, & am driuen away as the greshoppers.
My knees are weake thorow fastynge my flesh is dryed vp for want of fatnesse.
I am become a rebuke vnto them, they loke vpon me and shake their heades.
Helpe me, O Lorde my God, oh saue me for thy mercies sake.
That they maye knowe, how that thys is thy hand, and that thou hast done it.
Though they curse, yet blesse thou: and let them be confounded, that ryse vp agaynst me, but let thy seruaunt reioyse.
Let myne aduersaryes be clothed wyth their owne shame, as with a cloke.
As for me, I wyl geue thanckes vnto the Lord wyth my mouth, and praise hym among the multitude.
For he standeth at the ryght hand of the pore, to saue hym from suche as condempne hys soule.
110: A Psalme of Dauyd. The Lorde sayde vnto my Lord: Syt thou on my ryght hande, vntyll I make thyne enemies thy fotestole.
The Lord shal sende the rod of thy power out of Sion; be thou ruler euen in the myddest amonge thyne enemyes.
In the daye of thy power shal thy people offer the frewyll offerynges wyth an holye worshyppe, the dewe of thy byrthe is of the wombe of the mornynge.
The Lorde sware, and wyll not repente: Thou arte a priest for euer after the order of Melchisedec.
The Lorde vpon thy ryghte hande, shall smyte euen kinges in the daye of hys wrath.
He shall be iudge amonge the Heathen, he shall fyl them wyth deade bodyes, and smite in sunder the heades ouer diuerse countres.
He shall dryncke of the broke in the waye, therfore shall he lyft vp his head.
111: Prayse the euerlastynge. I wyll geue thanckes vnto the Lorde wyth my whole herte: secretly amonge the faythful and in the congregacyon:
The worckes of the Lorde are greate, sought oute of all them, that haue pleasure therin.
Hys worcke is worthy to be praysed and had in honoure, and his rightuousnes endureth for euer.
The mercyfull and gracyous Lord hath so done his maruelous workes, that they ought to be had in remembraunce.
He geueth meat vnto them, that feare him he is euer myndfull of hys couenaunte.
He sheweth hys people the power of hys worckes, that he may geue them the herytage of the Heathen.
The worckes of his hands are veryte and iudgment, all hys commaundementes are true.
They stand fast for euer and euer, and are done in truth and equyte.
He sent redempcyon vnto hys people, he hath commaunded his couenaunte for euer, holy and reuerente is his name
The feare of the Lorde is the beginning of wysdome, a good vnderstandyng haue al they that do therafter: the prayse of it endureth for euer.
112: Prayse the euerlastynge. Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord, and hath great delite in hys commaundementes.
Hys sede shal be mighty vpon earth the generacyon of the faythfull shalbe blessed.
Ryches and, plenteousnesse shalbe in hys house, and hys ryghtuousnesse endureth for euer.
Vnto the godly there aryseth vp lyghte in the darcknesse: he is mercyfull, louynge and ryghtuous.
Well is he that is mercyfull, and lendeth gladly, and pondereth his wordes wyth discrecyon,
For he shall neuer be moued, the ryghtuous shall be had in an euerlastynge remembraunce.
He wyll not be afrayed for anye euyll tydynges, his herte standeth fast, and beleueth in the Lord.
Hys hert is stablished, he wyl not shrynke, vntyl he se hys desyre vpon hys enemyes.
He hath sparsed abrode, and geuen to the poore, hys ryghtuousnes remayneth for euer his horne shalbe exealted with honoure
The vngodly shall se it, and it shall greue them: he shall gnash with his teeth, and consume awaye. and the desyre of the vngodlye shall perysh.
113: Prayse the euerlastynge. Prayse the Lord (O ye seruauntes) O prayse the name of the Lorde.
Blessed be the name of the lord, from this time forth euermore
The Lords name is worthy to be praysed from the risynge vp of the Sun vnto the going downe of the same.
The Lorde is hye aboue all Heathen, and his glory aboue the heauens.
Who is lyke vnto the Lorde oure God, that hath his dwellynge so hye,
whyche humbleth him selfe, to beholde that is in heauen and earth.
Which taketh vp the simple out of the dust and lyfteth the poore out of the myre.
That he may sette him amonge the prynces, euen amonge the prynces of hys people.
Whyche maketh the baren woman to kepe house, and to be a ioyfull mothere of chyldren. Prayse the euerlastyng.
114: When Israel came out of Egypt and the house of Iacob from among that straunge people.
Iuda was his Sanctuary, Israell his domynyon.
The sea saw that & fled, Iordan turned backe.
The mountaynes skipped like rammes, and the lytle hylles like yong shepe.
What ayled the, O thou sea, that thou fleddest so thou Iordan, that thou turnedest backe?
Ye mountaynes that ye skypped lyke rammes: and ye litle hilles, like yong shepe?
The earth trembled at the presence of the Lorde, at the presence of the God of Iacob.
Whyche turned the harde rocke into a staudynge water, and the flynte stone into a spryngyng well.
115: Not vnto vs, O Lorde not vnto vs. but vnto thy name geue the praise for thy louing mercye & faythfulnesse.
Wherfore shal the Heathen say wher is now their God?
As for oure God, he is in heauen, he doeth whatsoeuer it pleaseth him.
Their ymages are but syluer and gold, euen the worke of mens handes.
They haue mouthes, and speake not: eies haue they, but they se not.
Thei haue eares, and heare not: noses haue they, but they smell not.
They haue handes, and handle not, fete haue they, but they cannot goo, neyther can they speake thorow their throte.
They that made them, are lyke vnto them and so are all suche as put theyr truste in them.
But let Israell trust in the Lorde, for he is their succoure and defence.
Let the house of Aaron put their truste in the Lorde for he is their succoure and defence
They that feare the Lorde, lette them put their trust in the Lord, for he is their succour and defence.
The Lorde is myndfull of vs, and blesseth vs: he blesseth the house of Israel, he blesseth the house of Aaron.
Yea he blesseth al them that feare the Lord both smale and great.
The Lorde encrease you more and more: you, and your children.
For ye are the blessed of the Lord, whych made heauen and earth.
Al the whole heauens are the Lordes, but the earth hath he geuen vnto the chyldren of men.
The dead prayse not the (O Lorde) nether all they that go downe into sylence.
But we wil prayse the Lord, from this time forth for euermore. Prayse the euerlastynge.
116: I am wel pleased, that the Lord hath hearde the voyce of my prayer.
That he hath enclyned his eare vnto me, therfore wil I cal vpon him as long as I lyue.
The snares of death compased me round aboute, the paynes of hell gat hold vpon me I founde trouble and heauynesse.
Then called I vpon the name of the Lord O Lorde: delyuer my soule.
Gracious is the Lord, and rightuous, yea oure God is mercyfull.
The Lorde preserueth the symple, I was brought downe, and he helped me.
Turne agayne then vnto thy rest, O my soule, for the Lord hath geuen the thy desire.
And why thou haste delyuered my soule from death, myne eyes from teares, and my fete from fawlyng.
I wyll walcke before the Lorde, in the land of the lyuyng.
I beleued, and therfore haue I spoken, but I was sore troubled.
I sayde in my hast: Al men are liers.
What rewarde shall I geue vnto the Lorde, for all the benyfytes that he hath done vnto me?
I wyl receyue the, cuppe of saluacion, and call vpon the name of the Lord.
I wyll paye my vowes in the presence of al his people,
right deare in the syghte of the Lorde is the death of his saynctes.
O Lorde, I am thy seruaunt, I am thy seruant, and the son of thy handmaide, thou hast broken my bondes in sonder.
I wyl offre to the sacrifyce of thanckesgegeuynge, and wyll call vpon the name of the Lord.
I wyll paye my vowes vnto the Lord in the syght of al his people,
in the courtes of the Lordes house, euen in the middest of the, O Ierusalem. Prayse the euerlasting.
117: O prayse the Lorde all ye Gentyles, laude him al ye people.
For his mercyfull kyndnes is euer more and more toward vs, and the truth of the Lorde eudureth for euer. Prayse the euerlasting.
118: O geue thankes vnto the Lord, for he is gracyous, & hys mercy endureth for euer.
Let Israel now confesse, that his mercy eudureth for euer.
Let the house of Aaron now confesse, that his mercy endureth for euer.
Yea let them now that feare the Lorde confesse, that his mercy endureth for euer.
I called vpon the lord in trouble, and the lord heard me at large.
The lord is my helper, I wyll not feare what man doeth vnto me.
The lord is my helper, and I shall se my desyre vpon myne enemyes.
It is better to trust in the lord, then to put any cofydence in man.
It is better to trust in the lord then to put any confydence in prynces.
All Heathen compassed me round about but in the name of the lorde wyll I destroye them.
They kepe me in on euery side, but in the name of the lord, I wyll destroy them.
They came aboute me lyke bees, and wer as hote as the fyre in the thornes, but in the name of the Lorde I wyll destroye them.
They thrust at me, that I myght fall, but the lorde was my helpe.
The lorde is my strength, and my songe and is become my saluation.
The voice of ioy and meyth is in the dwellynges of the rightuous, for the ryght hand of the Lord hath gotten the victory.
The ryght hande of the Lord hath the preemynence, the ryght hande of the Lorde hath gotten the victory.
I wyll not dye, but lyue, and declare the workes of the lord.
The Lorde hath chastened and correcte me, but he hath not geuen me ouer vnto deathe.
Open me the gates of ryghtuousnes, that I maye go in there thorowe, and geue thanckes vnto the Lord.
This is the dore of the Lorde, the rightuous shall enter in thorow it.
I thancke, the that thou hast herd me, and are become my saluatyon.
The same stone whych the builders refused, is become the heade stone in the corner
Thys was the Lordes doynge, and it is maruelous in our eyes.
This is the, daye whych the Lorde hath made, let vs reioyse and be glad in it.
Helpe now O lord O, lord sende vs now prosperity.
Blessed be he that commeth in the name of the Lorde, we wysh you good lucke, ye that be of the house of the Lord.
God is the lord, and hath shewed vs light O garnysh the solempne feaste wyth grene braunches, euen vnto the hornes of the aulter.
Thou art my God, and I wil thancke the: thou art my God, and I wyll prayse the.
O geue thanckes vnto the lorde, for he is gracyous, and his mercy endureth for euer.
119: Aleph. Blessed are those that be vndefyled in the way: which walcke in the law of the Lord.
Blessed are they that kepe hys testimonies, and seke him with their whole herte.
Which walcke in hys wayes, and do no wickednes.
Thou haste geuen strayte charge to kepe thy commaundementes.
O that my wayes were stablished to kepe thy statutes.
So shoulde I not be confounded while I haue respecte vnto all thy commaundemente
I wyll thancke the wyth an vnfayned herte, because I am learned in the iudgmentes of thy ryghtuousnesse.
I wyll kepe thy statutes, O forsake me not vtterly.
Beth. Where withall shall a yonge man clense his waye? Euen by rulynge hym selfe after thy worde.
Wyth my whole herte do I seke the, O let me not go wronge out of thy commaundementes.
Thy wordes haue I hyd wythin my hert that I should not synne against the.
Praysed be thou O Lorde, O teache me thy statutes.
With my lippes wil I be tellyng out all the iudgmentes of thy mouth.
I haue as greate delyte in the way of thy the testimonies, as in al maner of ryches.
I wyl exercise my selfe in thy commaundementes, and haue respect vnto thy fotepathe
My delite shalbe in thy statutes, I wyll not forget thy wordes.
Gimel. O do well vnto thy seruant, that I maye lyue and kepe thy wordes.
Open thou myne eyes, and so shall I spy out wonderous thynges in thy lawe.
I am a straunger vpon earth, O hide not thy commaundementes fro me.
My soule breaketh out, for the very feruent desire that I haue alwaie vnto the iudgementes.
Thou rebukest the proud, cursed are they that departe from thy commaundementes.
O turne fro me shame and rebuke, for I kepe thy testimonies.
Princes also syt and speake against me but thy seruaunt is occupied in thy statutes.
In thy testomonyes is my delite, they are my councelers.
Deleth. My soule cleaueth to the dust, O quicken thou me accordyng to thy word.
I knowledged my waies, and thou herdest me, O teach me then thy statutes.
Make me to vnderstand the waye of thy commaundementes, and so shall I talcke of thy wonderous workes.
My soule melteth awaye for verye heuynesse, O set me vp accordyng vnto thy word
Take fro me the waye of lyeng, and graunte me thy lawe.
I haue chosen the way of truth, thy iudgementes haue I layed before me.
I stycke vnto thy testimonies, O Lorde confound me not.
I wyll runne the waye of thy commaundementes, when thou haste comforted my herte.
He. Teach me O lord the way of thy statutes and I shall kepe it vnto the ende.
O geue me vnderstandyng, & I shall kepe thy lawe, yea I shal kepe it wyth my whole herte.
Leade me in the pathe of thy commaundmentes, for that is my desyre,
Enclyne myne herte vnto thy testymonies, and not to couetousnes.
O turne awaye myne eyes, leste they behold vanite, and quycken me in thy way.
O stablish thy word in thy seruaunt, that I may feare the.
Take awaie the rebuke that I am afraied of, for thy iudgmentes are amyable.
Beholde, my delyte is in thy commaundementes, O quicken me in thy ryghtuousnesse.
Vau. Let thy louynge mercy come vnto me, O Lorde, and thy sauynge health accordynge vnto thy worde.
That I may geue answere vnto my blasphemers, for my trust is thy word.
O take not the worde of treuth vtterly out of my my mouthe, for my hope is in thy iudgementes.
So shall I alwaye kepe thy lawe, yea for euer and euer.
And I wyll walcke at lybertye, for I seke thy commaundementes.
I wyll speake of thy testimonyes euen before kynges, and wyll not be ashamed.
My delyte shalbe in thy commaundementes whych I loue.
My handes also wyll I lyft vp vnto thy commaundementes which I loue, and my talkinge shalbe of thy statutes.
Zain. O thyncke vpon thy seruaunt as concernynge thy worde, wherin thou haste caused me to put my trust.
For it is my comfort in my trouble, yea thy word quyckeneth me.
The proude haue me greatly in derysyon yet shryncke not I from thy law.
I remember thyne euerlasting iudgementes O Lorde, and am comforted.
I am horrible afraied for the vngodly, that forsake thy law.
Thy statutes are my songes in the house of my pylgremage.
I thyncke vpon thy name, O Lorde, in the nyghte esason, and kepe thy lawe.
It is mine owne, for I kepe thy commaundementes.
Heth Thou art my porcion, O lord, I am purposed to kepe thy law.
I make myne humble petycyon in thy presence wyth my whole herte, O be mercyfull vnto me accordynge vnto thy word.
I cal myne owne wayes to remembrance, and turne my fete into thy testimonies.
I make haste, and prolonge not the time, to kepe thy commaundementes.
The congregacyons of the vngodly haue robbed me, but I forget not thy law.
At midnight stand I vp, to geue thanckes vnto the, for the iudgmentes of thy ryghtuousnesse.
I am a companyon of all them that feare the, and kepe thy commaundementes.
The earth, O Lord, is ful of thy mercy. O teach me thy statutes.
Teh. O Lord, thou hast dealt frendly wyth thy seruaunt, according vnto thy word.
O learne me thy kyndnesse, nourtoure and knowlege, for I beleue thy commaundementes.
Before I was troubled, I wente wronge but now I kepe thy word.
Thou art good & frendly, O teach me the statutes.
The proud ymagyn lyes vpon me, but I kepe thy commaundementes with my whole herte.
Their herte is as fat as brawne, but my delyte is in thy law.
It is good for me that I haue bene in trouble, that I may learne thy statutes.
The law of thy mouth is dearer vnto me, then thousandes of golde and siluer.
Iod. Thy hands haue made me and fashyoned me, O geue me vnderstandyng, that I may learne thy commaundementes.
They that feare the, wyll be glad when they se me, because I put my truste in thy worde.
I knowe, O Lorde, that thy iudgmentes are right, and that thou of very faithfulnes hast caused me to be troubled.
O let thy mercyful kyndnesse be my comforte, accordynge to the promes that thou hast made vnto thy seruaunt.
O let thy louyng mercies come vnto me, that I may lyue, for thy law is my delite.
Let the proud be confounded, which handle me so falslye.
But let such as feare the, and knowe the testimonies, be turned vnto me.
O let myne herte be vndefyled in thy statutes that I be not ashamed.
Caph. My soule longeth for thy sauynge health, for my trust is in thy word,
Myne eyes long sore for thy word, saing: O when wylt thou comforte me?
For I am become like a botel in the smoke, yet do not I forget thy statutes.
How many are the dayes of thy seruaunt? When wilt thou be auenged of myne aduersaryes?
The proude haue dygged pyttes for me, which are not after thy lawe.
All thy commaundementes are true, they persecute me falsely, O be thou my helpe.
They haue almooste made an ende of me vpon earth, but I forsake not thy commaundementes.
O quycken me after thy louynge kyndenes, and so shall I kepe the testimonyes of thy mouth.
Lamed. O Lorde, thy worde endureth for euer in heauen.
Thy trueth also remayneth from one generacion to another: thou hast layed the foundacion of the earth, and it abydeth.
They contynue this daye accordinge too thyne ordinaunce, for all thinges serue the.
If my delyte were not in thy lawe, I should perysh in my trouble.
I will neuer forget thy commaundementes, for with them thou quickenest me.
I am thyne, Oh helpe me, for I seke thy commaundementes.
The vngodly laye wayte for me too destroye me, but I considre thy testimonyes.
I se that all thynges come to an ende, but thy commaundement is exeeadyng broade.
Mem. O what loue haue I vnto thy law? all the daye longe is my talkyng of it.
Thou thorow thy commaundement hast made me wyser then myne enemyes, for it is euer by me.
I haue more vnderstandyng then all my teachers, for thy testimonies are my studye.
Yea, I am wyser then the aged, for I kepe thy commaundementes.
I refrayne my fete from euery euell waye, that I maye kepe thy woordes.
I shrynke not from thy iudgementes, for thou teachest me.
O howe swete are thy woordes vnto my throte? Yea, more then hony vnto my mouth.
Thorow thy commaundementes I gette vnderstandynge, therefore I hate all false wayes.
Nun. Thy woorde is a lanterne vnto my fete and a light vnto my pathes.
I haue sworne and am stedfastly purposed, to kepe the iudgementes of thy righteousnesse.
I am troubled aboue measure, quycken me, O Lord, according vnto thy worde.
Let the frewill offeringes of my mouthe please the, O Lorde, and teache me thy iudgementes.
My soule is alwaye in my hande, yet do not I forget thy lawe.
The vngodly haue layed a snare for me, but yet swarue not I from thy commaundmentes.
Thy testimonyes haue I claymed as myne heritage for euer: and why? thei are the very ioye of my herte.
I applye myne herte to fulfil thy statutes alwaye, euen vnto the ende.
Samech. I hate the vngodly, but thy law do I loue.
Thou art my defence & shylde, my truste is in thy woorde.
Away fro me ye wycked, I will kepe the commaundementes of my God.
O stablish me according vnto thy worde, that I maye lyue, & let me not be disapoynted of my hope.
Holde thou me vp, and I shall be safe: yea I shall euer be talkyng of thy statutes.
Thou treadest doune all them that departe from thy statutes, for they ymagin but disceate.
Thou puttest awaye all the vngodly of the earth lyke drosse, therfore I loue thy testymonies,
My flesh trembleth for feare of the, and I am afrayed of thy iudgementes.
Ain. I deale wt the thinge that is lawfull & ryght, O geue me not ouer vnto mine oppressours.
Be thou suertye for thy seruaunte too do hym good, that the proude do me no wronge.
Myne eyes are waysted awaye with lokyng for thy health, and for the worde of thy righteousnesse.
O deale with thy seruaunt according vnto thy louing mercy, & teach me thy statutes.
I am thy seruaunt, O graunte me vnderstanding, that I may know thy testimonies.
It is tyme for the (O Lord) to lay to thine hande, for they haue destroyed thy lawe.
For I loue thy commaundementes aboue golde and precious stone.
Therfore holde I streyght all thy commaundementes, and all false wayes I vtterly abhorre.
Phe. Thy testimonyes are wonderfull, therefore doth my soule kepe them.
When thy woorde goeth forthe, it geueth light & vnderstandyng, euen vnto babes.
I open my mouth and draw in my breath, for I desyre thy commaundementes.
O loke thou vpon me, & be mercifull, as thou vsest to do vnto those that loue thy name.
Ordre my goinges after thy woorde that no wickednesse raygne in me.
O delyuer me from the wrongeous dealinges of men, and so shall I kepe thy commaundementes.
Shewe the light of thy countenaunce vnto thy seruaunt, and learne me thy statutes.
Myne eyes gusshe out with water, because men kepe not thy lawe.
Zade. Ryghteous art thou, O Lorde, and true is thy judgement.
Thy testimonyes that thou hast commaunded are exceadyng, righteous and true.
My zeale hath euen consumed me, because myne enemyes haue forgotten thy wordes.
Thy worde is tryed to the vttermost, and thy seruaunt loueth it.
I am small and of no reputacion, yet do not I forget thy commaundementes.
Thy righteousnesse is an euerlastyng righteousnes, and thy lawe is true.
Trouble and heuynesse haue taken holde vpon me, yet is my delite in thy commaundementes.
The righteousnes of thy testimonyes is euerlastyng, O graunt me vnderstandinge, and I shall lyue.
Koph. I call with my whole herte, heare me, O Lorde, I will kepe thy statutes.
Yea, euen vpon the do I call, helpe me, & I shall kepe thy testimonies.
Early in the mornyng do I crye vnto the, for in thy worde is my trust.
Myne eyes preuente the night watches, that I might be occupyed in thy wordes.
Heare my voyce, O Lorde, accordynge vnto thy louyng kyndnesse, quycken me accordyng as thou art wont.
They drawe nye that of malyce persecute me, and are farre from thy lawe.
Be thou nye at hande also, O Lorde, for thy promyses are faythfull.
As concernynge thy testimonies, I haue knowen euer sens the beginnuing, that thou hast grounded them for euer.
Res. O considre myne aduersite, & deliuer me, for I do not forget thy lawe.
Manteyn thou my cause and defende me, quycken me according vnto thy worde.
Health is farre from the vngodly, for thei regarde not thy statutes.
Great is thy mercy, O Lorde, quicken me as thou art wont.
Many there are that trouble me, & persecute me, yet do not I swarue from thy testimonies.
It greueth me, when I se, that the transgressours kepe not thy law.
Considre, O Lorde, how I loue thy commaundementes, O quycken me with thy louyng kyndnesse.
Thy worde is true from euerlastyng, all the iudgementes of thy righteousnesse endure for euer more.
Sin. The princes persecute me withoute cause, but my herte standeth in awe of thy woordes.
I am as gladde of thy worde, as one that fyndeth great spoyles.
As for lyes, I hate and abhorre them, but thy law do I loue.
Seuen times a daye do I prayse the, because of thy righteous iudgementes.
Great is the peace that they haue whych loue thy law, and they are not offended at it.
Lord, I loke for thy sauynge healthe, and do after thy commaundementes.
My soule kepeth thy testimonies, and loueth them exceadingly.
I kepe thy commaundementes and testimonies, for all my wayes are before the.
Thau. Let my complaynte come before the, O Lorde, geue me vnderstanding, accordynge vnto thy worde.
Oh let my supplicacion come before the, deliuer me according to thy promes.
My lyppes shall speake of thy prayse, seyng thou hast taught me thy statutes.
Yea, my tonge shall synge of thy worde, for all thy commaundementes are right.
Let thine hande helpe me, for I haue chosen thy commaundementes.
I longe for thy sauyng health, O Lorde, and in thy law is my delyte.
Oh let my soule lyue and prayse the, that thy iudgementes maye helpe me.
I go astraye, lyke a shepe that is lost: Oh seke thy seruaunt, for I do not forget thy commaundementes.
120: The song of the steares When I am in trouble, I cal vpon the Lorde, and he answereth me.
Delyuer my soule, O Lord from liyng lippes, and from a disceatful tonge.
What rewarde shalbe geuen or done vnto the, thou false tonge.
Euen myghty and sharpe arowes, wyth hote burnynge coales.
Who is me that my banyshmente endureth so longe: I dwel in the tabernacles of the sorowfull.
My soule hath long dwelt amonge them that be enemies vnto peace,
I laboured for peace, but when I spake therof, they made them to battayle.
121: The song of the steares. I lyft vp myne eyes vnto the hylles, from whence commeth my helpe.
My helpe commeth euen from the Lord which hath made heauen and earth.
He wyll not suffer thy fote to be moued, and he that kepeth the slepeth not.
Beholde, he that kepeth Israell, doth nether slomber nor slepe.
The Lorde him selfe is thy keper, the Lorde is thy defence vpon thy ryght hande.
So that the sunne shall not burne the by daye, nether the mone by nyght.
The Lorde preserueth the from all euyll, yea it is the Lorde that kepeth thy soule.
The Lorde preserueth thy goyng out and thy commynge in, from thys tyme forth for euer more.
122: The songe of the steares. I was glad, when they sayed vnto me: we wyll go into the house of the Lorde.
Oure fete shall stande in thy gates O Ierusalem.
Ierusalem is buylded as a cytye, that is at vnyte in it selfe.
For ther the tribes go vp, euen the tribes of the Lorde: to testyfye vnto Israel, to geue thanckes vnto the name of the Lorde.
For there is the seate of iudgmente, euen the seate of the house of Dauyd.
O praye for the peace of Ierusalem, they shall prospere that loue the.
Peace be wyth thy walles, and plenteousnes within thy palaces.
For my brethren and companions sakes, I wyll wysh the prosperite.
Yea because of the house of the Lord oure God, I wyll seke to do the good.
123: The songe of the steares. Vnto the lyft I vp mine eies, thou that dwelleste in the heauens.

Beholde euen, as the eyes of seruauntes loke vnto the handes of their maysters: and as the eyes of a maiden vnto the handes of her mastresse, euen so oure eyes wayte vpon the Lorde our God vntylll he haue mercy vpon vs.
Haue mercy vpon vs, O Lord, haue mercy vpon vs, for we are vtterly despysed.
Our soule is filled with the scornefull reprofe of the welthy, and wyth the despitefulnes of the proude.
124: The songe of the steares. If the Lord had not bene of oure side (now may Israel say)
If the Lord had not bene of oure syde when men rose vp against vs.
They had swalowed vs vp quicke when thei were so wrathfully displeased at vs.
Yea the waters had drowned vs, the streame had gone ouer oure soule.
The depe waters of the proud had gon euen vnto our soule.
But praysed be the Lord, which hath not geuen vs ouer for a praie vnto their teeth.
Oure soule is escaped, euen as a byrde out of the snare of the fouler: the snare is broken and we are delyuered.
Oure helpe standeth in the name of the Lord, which hath made heauen and earth.
125: The song of the steares. They that put their truste in the Lord, are euen as the mounte Syon, which may not be remoued, but standeth fast for euer.
The hylles stande about Ierusalem, euen so standeth the Lorde rounde about hys people, from this tyme forthe for euermore.
That the rodd of the vngodly come not into the lot of the righteous, lest the righteous put their hande vnto wickednesse.
Do wel, O Lord, vnto those that be good and true of herte.
As for suche as turne backe vnto their owne wickednesse, the Lorde shall leade them forth with the euell doers: but peace be vpon Israell.
126: The songe of the steares. When the Lorde turneth agayn the captiuitie of Syon, then shall we be lyke vnto them that dreame.
Then shal our mouth be filled wyth laughter, and oure tonge with ioye. Then shall it be sayd among the Heathen: the Lord hath done greate thynges for them.
Yea, the Lorde hath done greate thynges for vs all ready, wherof we reioyse.
Turne oure captiuitie, O Lorde, as the ryuers in the south.
They that sowe in teares, shall reape in ioye.
He that now goeth in hys waye wepyng and beareth forthe good sede, shall come agayne with ioye, & bryng hys sheaues wyth hym.
127: The song of the steares. Except the Lord buylde the house, their laboure is but loste that buylde it. Except the Lord kepe the cytye, the watchman waketh but in vayne.
It is but lost labour that ye ryse vp early and take no rest, but eate the breade of carefulnesse: for loke to whom it pleaseth him, he geueth it in slepe.
Lo, chyldren & the frute of the wombe are an heritage & gift, that commeth of the Lorde.
Lyke as the arrowes in the hande of the gyaunt, euen so are the yonge chyldren.
Happy is the man, that hathe his quyuerful of them: they shal not be ashamed, when they speake with their enemyes in the gate.
128: The song of the steares. Blessed are all they that feare the Lord, & walke in his wayes.
For thou shalte eate the laboures of thyne owne handes: O well is the, happy art thou.
Thy wyfe shalbe as the frutefull vyne vpon the walles of thy house. Thy chyldren lyke the Olyue braunches rounde about thy table.
Lo, thus shal the man be blessed, that feareth the lorde.
The lord shall so blesse the out of Syon, that thou shalt se Hierusalem in prosperytie all thy lyfe longe.
Yea, that thou shalt se thy chylders chyldren, and peace vpon Israel.
129: The song of the steares. Many tyme haue they foughte agaynst me fro my youth vp (may Israel now saye.)
Yea, many a tyme haue they fought gaainst me fro my youth vp, but thei haue not ouercome me.
The plowers plowed vpon my backe, & made longe forowes.
But the righteous lorde hath hewen the yocke of the vngodly in peces.
Let them be confounded & turned backewarde, as many as haue euell will at Syon.
Let them be euen as the haye vppon the house toppes, whyche wythereth afore it be pluckte vp.
Wherof the mower fylleth not his hande, neither he that byndeth vp the sheaues, hys bosome.
So that they which go by, saye not so much as: the Lord prospere you, we wish you good lucke in the name of the Lord.
130: The song of the steares. Ovt of the depe cal I vnto the O Lord,
Lord heare my voice Oh let thyne eares consider wel the voice of my complaint
If thou Lorde wylte be extreme to marke what is done amysse. Oh Lord who may abide it?
But ther is mercy wyth the, that thou maiest be feared.
I loke for the Lord, my soule doth wayte for hym, and in his word is my trust.
My soule doth paciently abide the Lorde from the one morning to the other.
Let Israel trust in the Lord, for wyth the Lorde there is mercy and plenteouse redempcyon.
And he shal redeme Israel from al his synnes.
131: The songe of the steares. Lorde, I am not hye mynded, I haue no proude lokes. I do not exercise my selfe in greate matters, whych are hye for me.
But I refrayne my soule and kepe it lowlye as a childe that is weaned from his mother: yea my soule is euen as a weaned child
Let Israel trust in the Lord, from this time forth for euermore.
132: The song of the steares. Lorde, remember Dauyd and all his trouble.
How he swore vnto the Lorde, and vowed a vowe vnto the allmyghty one of Iacob:
I wyll not come within the tabernacle of my house, nor clyme vp in my bedde.
I wyll not suffer myne eyes to slepe, nor myne eye lyddes to slomber.
Vntill I fynde out a place for the Lorde, an habitacion for the mightye one of Iacob.
Lo we herde of the same at Ephrata, and found it in the woode.
We wyll go into hys tabernacle, and fall downe before his fote stole.
Aryse, O Lord, into thy restynge place, thou and the arcke of thy strength.
Let thy Preastes be clothed wyth rightuousnesse, and let thy saynctes reioyse.
For thy seruaunte Dauyds sake turne not awaye the presence of thyne anoynted.
The Lord hath made a faythful ooth vnto Dauyd, and he shall not shrynke from it Of the frute of thy body shal I set vpon thy seate.
If thy chyldren wyll kepe my couenaunt, and my testimony that I shal lerne them: their chyldren also shal syt vpon thy seate for euermore.
For the Lord hath chosen Syon, to be an habitacyon for him selfe hath he chosen her.
This shalbe my rest, here wyll I dwel for I haue a delyte therin.
I wyll blesse her vytalles wyth increase, and wyll satysfye her poore with bread.
I wyl decke her Preastes with health and her saynctes shall reioyse and be glad.
Ther shall I make the horne of Dauid to floryshe, I haue ordeyned a lanterne for myne anoynted.
As for hys enemyes, I shall clothe them wyth shame, but vpon hym selfe shall hys crowne florysh.
133: The song of the steares of Dauyd. Behold, how good and ioyfull a thinge it is, brethren to dwel together in vnitie.
It is like the preacious oyntment vpon the heade, that ranne downe vnto the beard: euen vnto Aarons bearde, and wente downe to the skyrtes of his clothyng.
Like the dewe of Hermon, which fell vpon the hil of Sion. For there the Lorde promysed hys blesyng, and lyfe for euermoe.
134: The song of the steares Behold, O praise the Lord, al ye seruantes of the Lorde, ye that by night stande in the house of the Lord.
O lyfte vp youre handes in the Sanctuary, and prayse the Lorde.
The lorde that made heauen and earthe blesse the out of Sion.
135: Prayse the euerlastynge. O praise the name of the Lord prayse it O ye seruauntes of the Lorde.
Ye that stande in the house of the Lorde, in the courtes of the house of our God.
O prayse the lord for the lord is gracious: O sing prayses vnto hys name, for it is louely.
For why the Lorde hath chosen Iacob vnto hym selfe, and Israel for his owne possession.
For I know that the Lorde is greate, and that our Lorde is aboue all goddes.
Whatsoeuer the Lord pleaseth that doth he in heauen and in earth, in the sea, and in all deape places.
He bryngeth forth the cloudes from the endes of the worlde, he turneth the lyghtenynges vnto rayne, bryngynge the wyndes out of their treasuryes.
Which smote the fyrst borne of Egypte both of man and of beast.
He hath sent tokens and wonders into the middest of the, O thou lande of Egypt, vpon Pharao and al his seruauntes.
Whych smote dyuerse nacyons, and slew myghty Kynges.
Sehon Kynge of the Amorytes, Og the Kynge of Basan, and all the Kyngdomes of Canaan.
And gaue their land for an heritage, for an heritage vnto Israel his people.
Thy name. O Lorde, endureth for euer, so doeth thy memoryall, O Lorde, from one generacyon to another.
For the Lorde wil auenge his people, and be gracyous vnto hys seruauntes.
As for the ymages of the Heathen, they are but siluer and golde, the worcke of mens handes.
They haue mouthes, and speake not: eyes haue they, but they se not.
They haue eares, and yet they heare not, neyther is ther any breath in their mouthes.
They that make them, are lyke vnto them, and so are all they that put their trust in them.
Prayse the Lord ye house of Israel, praise the Lorde ye house of Aaron.
Prayse the Lorde, ye house of Leui, ye that feare the Lorde, prayse the Lorde.
Praysed be the Lord out of Sion, whych dwelleth at Ierusalem. Praise the euerlastynge.
136: O geue thankes vnto the Lord, for he is gracious, and his mercy endureth for euer.
O geue thankes vnto the God of all goddes, for his mercy endureth for euer.
O thancke the Lord of all Lordes, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Whych only doth greate wonders, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Which by hys wisdome made the heauens for his mercy endureth for euer.
Which layed out the earth aboue the waters, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Whych hath made great lyghtes, for hys mercy endureth for euer.
The sunne to rule the daye, for hys mercy endureth for euer.
The mone and the starres to gouerne the nyght, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Whych smote Egypt wyth their fyrste borne, for his mercy endureth for euer.
And brought out Israell from among them, for his mercy endureth for euer.
With a myghtye hand and stretcheth out arme, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Whych deuyded the reed sea into partes, for his mercy endureth for euer.
And made Israell to go thorow the myddest of it, for his mercy endureth for euer.
But as for Pharao, and his host, he ouerthrewe them in the read sea, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Which led hys people thorow the wyldernesse, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Whiche smote greate Kynges, for hys mercy endureth for euer.
Yea, and slue myghtye Kynges, for hys mercy endureth for euer.
Sehon Kyng of the Amorytes, for hys mercy endureth for euer.
And Og the Kyng of Basan, for his mercy endureth for euer.
And gaue awaye their lande for an herytage, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Euen for an heritage vnto Israel hys seruaunt, for his mercy endureth for euer.
Which remembreth vs, when we are in trouble, for hys mercy endureth for euer.
Which geueth fode vnto al flesh, for his mercy endureth for euer.
O geue thankes vnto the God of heauen, for his mercy endureth for euer.
137: By the waters of Babylon we sat downe and weapte, when we remembred Syon.
As for our harpes, we hanged them vpon the trees, that are therin.
Then they that led vs awaye captyue, requyred of vs a songe and melody in our heauynes: synge vs one of the songes of Syon.
How shall we synge the Lordes songe in a straunge land?
If I forget the, O Ierusalem, let my right hande be forgotten.
If I do not remember the, lette my tonge cleue to the rofe of my mouth: yea, if I preferre not Ierusalem in my myrth.
Remember the children of Edom, O Lorde in the daye of Ierusalem, howe they sayde: doune wyth it, doune wyth it: euen to the grounde.
O daughter of Babilon, thou shalt come to mysery thyselfe: yea, happye shall he be, that rewardeth the as thou hast serued vs.
Blessed shall he be, that taketh thy chyldren, and throweth them agaynst the stones.
138: Of Dauid. I wyll geue thankes vnto the. O Lord, wyth my whole herte, euen before the Gods, wil I singe prayses vnto the.
I wyll worshyp toward thy holy temple and prayse thy name, because of thy louyng kyndenesse and trueth, for thou hast magnyfyed thy worde, accordyng vnto thy greate name.
When I call vpon the, thou hearest me, & endewest my soule wyth muche strength.
All the Kynges of the earthe shall prayse the, O Lord, when they heare the wordes of thy mouth.
Yea, they shall singe in the wayes of the Lorde, that great is the glory of the Lord.
For though the Lorde be hye, yet hath he respecte vnto the lowly: as for the proude, he beholdeth theim a farre of.
Though I walke in the middest of trouble, yet shalte thou refreshe me: thou shalte stretche forth thyne hande vpon the furiousnes of myne enemyes, and thy righte hande shall saue me.
The Lord shall make good for me, yea, thy mercy, O LORDE, endureth for euer despyse not then the worcke of thyne awne handes.
139: To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid. O Lorde, thou searchest me out, and knowest me.
Thou knowest my doune sittyng and myne vprysinge, thou vnderstandest my thoughtes a farre of.
Thou art about my path & about my bed and spyest out all my wayes.
For lo, there is not a worde in my tonge, but thou, O Lorde knowest it altogether.
Thou hast fashioned me behynde and before, and layed thyne hande vpon me.
Such knowlege is to wonderfull and excellent for me, I can not atteyne vnto it.
Whither shal I go then from thy sprete? or, whyther shall I go then frome thy presence?
If I clyme vp into heauen, thou art there if I go doune to hel, thou art there also.
If I take the wynges of the mornynge, & remayne in the vttermost parte of the sea:
Euen there also shall thy hande leade me, and thy right hand shall holde me.
If I saye: peraduenture the darkenesse shall couer me, then shall my nyghte be turned to daye.
Yea, the darkenesse is no darkenesse with the, but the nyght is as cleare as the day, the darkenesse and light are both a lyke.
For my reynes are thyne, thou hast couered me in my mothers wombe.
I will geue thankes vnto the, for I am wonderously made: maruelous are thy workes, & that my soule knoweth right well.
My bones are not hyd from the, though I be made secretly, and fashyoned beneth in the earth.
Thyne eyes se myne vnperfectnesse, they stande all written in thy boke: my dayes were fashyoned, when as yet there was not one of them.
How deare are thy counsails vnto me O God? O how greate is the summe of them?
If I tell them, they are mo in numbre then the sande: when I wake vp, I am presente with the.
Wylt thou not slaye the wycked (Oh God) that the bloudthyrsty myghte departe fro me?
For they speake vnright of the, thyne enemyes exalte them selfes presumpteously.
I hate them, O Lorde, that hate the: and I maye not awaye wyth those that ryse vp agaynst the.
Yea I hate them right sore, therefore are they myne enemyes.
Trye me, O God, and seke the grounde of myne herte: proue me, and examen my thoughtes.
Loke well if there be any way of wickednesse in me, and leade me in the way euerlastynge.
140: To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid. Deliuer me, O Lorde, from the euel men, Oh preserue me from the wycked men.
Which ymagin mischief in their hertes, and stere vp strife all the daye longe.
They sharpen their tonges lyke a serpent: adders poyson is vnder their lippes. Selah.
Kepe me, O Lorde, from the hande of the vngodly: preserue me from the wycked men, which are purposed to ouerthrowe my goynges.
The proude haue layed a snare for me, & spred a net abroade wyth coardes, yea, and set trappes in my waye. Selah.
But my sayinge is vnto the Lorde: thou art my God, heare the voyce of my prayer O Lord.
O Lord God, thou strength of my health thou hast couered my head in the day of battayle.
Let not the vngodly haue hys desyre, O Lord, let him not haue hys purpose, lest they be to proude. Selah.
Let the mischief of their owne lippes fall vpon the head of theym, that compase me about.
Let hote burnyng coales fall vpon them let them be cast into the fyre, & into the pytte, that they neuer ryse vp agayne.
A man full of woordes shall not prospere vpon the earth: a malicious & wicked person shalbe hunted awaye, and destroyed.
Sure I am, that the Lorde wyll auenge the poore, & maynteyne the cause of the helpelesse.
The righteous also shall geue thanckes vnto thy name, and the iust shall continue in thy sight.
141: A Psalme of Dauid. Lorde, I call vpon the: hast the vnto me, & consider my voyce, when I crye vnto the.
Let my prayer be setforth in thy sight as the incense, and let the lifting vp of my handes be an euenynge sacrifice.
Set a watch, O lorde, before my mouth, yea, a watch at the dore of my lippes.
O let not myne herte be enclyned to any euell thyng, to be mynded as the vngodly or wicked men, lest I eate of suche thynges as please them.
Let the righteous rather smite me frindly, & reproue me: so will I take it, as though he had poured oyle vpon my head: it shall not hurt my head, yea, I will praye yet for theyr wickednesse.
Their iudges stomble at the stone, yet heare they my wordes, that they be ioyfull.
Oure bones lye scatered before the pyt, lyke as when one graueth and dyggeth vp the grounde.
But myne eyes loke vnto the, O Lorde God: in the is my trust, Oh caste not out my soule.
Kepe me from the snare whiche they haue layed for me, and from the trappes of the wicked doers.
Let the vngodly fall into their owne nettes together, vntyll I be gone by them.
142: The instruccion of Dauid, a prayer when he was in the caue. I crye vnto the Lorde with my voyce, yea, euen vnto the Lord do I make my supplicacion.
I poure out my complaynte before hym, and shewe hym of my trouble.
When my sprete is in heuynesse, for thou knowest my path: in the way wherin I walke haue they preuely layed a snare for me.
I loke vpon my right hande, & se, there is no man that will know me. I haue no place to fle vnto, no man careth for my soule.
Therfore do I crye vnto the, O Lorde, & say: thou art my hope and my porcion in the londe of the liuing.
Considre my complaynt, for I am brought very lowe. O deliuer me fro my persecuters, for thei are to stronge for me.
Bryng my soule out of pryson, that I may geue thankes vnto thy name: which thyng if thou wilt graunt me, then shall the righteous resorte vnto my company.
143: A Psalme of Dauid. Heare my prayer, O Lord, considre my desire: aunswere me for thy trueth and righteousnesse sake.
And entre not into iudgement with thy seruaunt, for in thy sighte shall no man lyuyng be iustefied.
For the enemye persecuteth my soule, he smyteth my lyfe doune too the grounde, he layeth me in the darkenesse, as the dead men of the worlde.
Therefore is my sprete vexed within me, and my herte within me is desolate.
Yet do I remembre the times past, I muse vpon all thy workes, yea, I exercise my selfe in the workes of thy handes.
I stretche forthe myne handes vnto the, my soule cryeth vnto the oute of the thyrstye lande. Selah.
Heare me, O Lorde, & that soone, for my sprete waxeth faynte: hyde not thy face fro me, lest I be lyke vnto theym that go doune into the graue.
O let me heare thy louyng kyndnesse by tymes in the morning, for in the is my trust: shew thou me the waye that I should walke in, for I lift vp my soule vnto the.
Deliuer me, O Lord, fro myne enemies, for I resorte vnto the.
Teache me to do the thynge that pleaseth the, for thou arte my God: lette thy louinge sprete leade me forth vnto the lande of righteousnes.
Quicken me, O Lord, for thy names sake and for thy righteousnesse sake brynge my soule out of trouble.
And of thy goodnesse scater myne enemyes abroade, & destroye all them that vexe my soule, for I am thy seruaunt.
144: Of Dauid. Blessed be the Lorde my refuge which teacheth my handes to warre, and my fyngers too fyght.
My hope and my castell, my defence and my deliuerer, my shylde in whome I trust, which gouerneth the people that is vnder me.
Lorde what is man, that thou hast suche respect vnto hym? Or the sonne of man, that thou so regardest hym?
Man is like a thing of naught, hys tyme passeth awaye like a shadow.
Bowe thy heauens, O Lorde, & come doune, touche the mountaynes, that thei may smoke with all.
Sende forthe the lightenynge and scater them, shute out thyne arrowes, and consume them.
Sende doune thyne hande from aboue, deliuer me, & take me out of the greate waters, from the hande of straunge chyldren.
Whose mouth talketh of vanitie, & theyr right hande is a right hande of falsede,
That I maye singe a new songe vnto the O God, and singe prayses vnto the vpon a tenstrynged lute.
Thou that geuest victory vnto kynges, & hast deliuered Dauid thy seruaunt from the parell of the swerde.
Saue me, and deliuer me from the hande of straunge chyldren, whose mouth talketh of vanitie, and their ryght hande is a ryghte hande of falsede.
That oure sonnes maye growe vp as the yong plantes, & that our daughters may be as the polyshed corners of the temple.
That oure garners may be full and plenteous with all maner of stoare: that oure shepe maye brynge forth thousandes and hundreth thousandes in our vyllages.
That our oxen may be strong to laboure, that there be no mischaunce, no decaye, & no complaynyng in our stretes.
Happy are the people that be in suche a case: yea, blessed are the people, whiche haue the Lord for their God.
145: A prayse of Dauid. I wyll magnifie the, O God my kyng, I wil prayse thy name for euer & euer.
Euery daye wil I geue thankes vnto the, & praise thy name for euer and euer.
Great is the Lord, & maruelous worthy to be praysed, there is no ende of his greatenesse.
One generacion shall prayse thy workes vnto another, and declare thy power.
As for me I will be talkynge of thy worshyp, thy glory, thy prayse, and wonderous workes.
So that men shal speake of the myght of thy maruelous actes, and tell of thy greatenes.
The memorial of thyne aboundant kyndnes shalbe shewed, & men shall synge of thy righteousnesse.
The Lord is gracious and merciful, longe sufferyng, and of great goodnesse.
The Lorde is louynge vnto euery man, & hys mercy is ouer all hys workes.
All thy workes prayse the (O Lorde) and thy saynctes geue thankes vnto the.
They shew the glory of the kyngdome, & talke of thy power.
That thy power, thy glory & mightinesse of thy kyngedome myghte be knowen vnto men.
Thy kyngdome is an euerlastyng kyngedome, and thy dominion endureth thorowe out all ages.
The Lord vpholdeth all such as shoulde fall, and lifteth vp all those that be doune.
The eyes of all wayte vpon the, and thou geuest them their meate in due season.
Thou openest thyne hande, and fyllest all thinges liuing with plenteousnesse.
The Lord is righteous in all his wayes, and holy in all hys workes.
The Lord is nye vnto them that call vpon him, yea, al such as call vpon hym faithfully.
He fulfilleth the desire of them that feare him, he heareth their crie, and helpeth them.
The Lord preserueth all theym that loue hym, but scatreth abroade all the vngodly.
My mouth shall speake the prayse of the Lord, and let all flesh geue thankes vnto his holy name for euer and euer. Prayse the euerlastynge.
146: Prayse the euerlastyng. Prayse the Lorde, O my soule:
whyle I lyue will I prayse the Lorde: yea, as longe as I haue any beyng, I will sing prayses vnto my God.
O put not your trust in prynces, nor in any chylde of man, for there is no helpe in them.
For when the breath of man goeth forth, he shall turne agayne to his earth, and so all hys thoughtes perysh.
Blessed is he that hath the God of Iacob for his helpe, and whose hope is in the Lord hys God.
Which made heauen and earth, the sea, & all that therin is, which kepeth hys promise for euer.
Which helpeth them to righte that suffre wrong, which fedeth the hongry. The Lord louseth men out of pryson,
the Lord geueth sight to the blynde. The Lorde helpeth them vp that are fallen, the Lord loueth the righteous.
The Lorde careth for the straungers, he defendeth the fatherlesse and wydow: as for the way of the vngodly, he turneth it vpside doune.
The Lord thy God, O Syon, is kyng for euermore, & thorow out all generacions. Prayse the euerlastynge.
147: Prayse the euerlastyng. O prayse the Lord, for it is a good thyng to sing prayses vnto our God: yea, a ioyful & pleasaunt thing is it to be thankeful.
The Lorde shall buylde vp Hierusalem, & gather together the outcastes of Israel.
He healeth the contryte in herte, and byndeth vp their woundes.
He telleth the numbre of the starres, and calleth them all by their names.
Great is our Lord, & great is his power: yea, hys wysdome is infinitie.
The Lord setteth vp the meke, and bryngeth the vngodly doune to the grounde.
O singe vnto the Lorde with thankesgeuyng, sing prayses vpon the harpe vnto our God.
Which couereth the heauen wyth cloudes, prepareth rayn for the earth, & maketh the grasse to growe vpon the mountaynes.
Which geueth fodre vnto the cattell, and fedeth the yong rauens that call vpon hym.
He hath no pleasure in the strengthe of an horse, neither deliteth he in any mans legges.
But the Lordes delyte is in them that feare hym, and put their trust in his mercy.
Prayse the Lord O Ierusalem, prayse thy God O Sion.
For he maketh fast the barres of the gates, and blesseth the chyldren within the.
He maketh peace in thy borders, & filleth the with the floure of wheate.
He sendeth forth hys commaundemente vpon earth, his worde runneth swyftly.
He geueth snow lyke wolle, & scatereth the hore frost lyke ashes.
He casteth forth hys yse lyke morsels, who is able to abyde hys frost?
He sendeth out hys woorde and mealteth them, he bloweth with hys wynd, & the waters flowe.
He sheweth hys woorde vnto Iacob, hys statutes and ordinaunces vnto Israel.
He hath not dealte so with all the Heathen, neither haue they knowlege of hys lawes. Prayse the euerlastyng.
148: Prayse the euerlastyng. O prayse the Lorde of heauen, prayse hym in the heygth.
Prayse hym all ye aungels of hys, prayse hym all hys hoost.
Prayse hym Sunne and Moone, prayse hym all ye starres and light.
Prayse hym all ye heauens, and ye waters that be vnder the heauens.
Let them prayse the name of the Lorde, for he commaunded, and they were made.
He hath made them fast for euer and euer, he hath geuen them a lawe whiche shall not be broken.
Prayse the Lord vpon earth, ye whalfysshes, and al depes.
Fyre and hayle, snow and vapors, wynde and storme, fulfillynge his worde.
Mountaynes and al hilles, fruteful trees and all Cedres.
Beastes and cattel, wormes and fethered foules.
Kynges of the earth and all people, Prynces and iudges of the worlde.
Yonge men and maydens, olde men and chyldren:
let them prayse the name of the Lord, for his name only is excellent, and his prayse aboue heauen and earth.
He exalteth the horne of his people, all hys saynctes shall prayse hym, the chyldren of Israell, euen the people that serueth him. Prayse the euerlastyng.
149: Prayse the euerlastynge. O synge vnto the Lorde a newe songe, let the congregacion of saynctes prayse hym.
Let Israell reioyse in hym that made hym, & let the chyldren of Sion be ioyfull in their kyng.
Let them prayse his name in the daunce, let them singe prayses vnto hym with tabrettes and harpes.
For the Lorde hath pleasure in hys people, and helpeth the meke harted.
Let the saynctes be ioyfull with glory, let them reioyse in their beddes.
Let the prayses of God be in their mouth and sharpe swerdes in their handes.
To be auenged of the Heathen, and to rebuke the people.
To bynde their Kynges in cheynes, and their nobles with lynckes of yron.
That they may be auenged of them, as it is written, such honour haue all his saynctes. Prayse the euerlastynge.
150: Prayse the euerlastyng. O prayse the Lord in his Sanctuary, prayse hym in the fyrmament of hys power.
Prayse hym in his noble actes, prayse him in hys excellent greatnesse.
Prayse hym in the sounde of the trompet, prayse hym vpon the lute and harpe.
Prayse hym in the cymbales and daunse prayse hym vpon the strynges and pype.
Prayse hym vpon the weltuned cymbals prayse him vpon the loude cymbales.
Let euery thing that hath breth, prayse the Lorde. Prayse the euerlastynge.
